docs.text:
Build or copy, validate and execute a GOLEM input against a WBGeo mesh.

If image_name is provided: Input and mesh files are copied into a directory in a named container, results are copied back after the run, and the container (including its temporary directory) is removed.

:param problem: may be an automatically generated hydrothermal/simple-reservoir problem or a GolemCustomBuilder containing complete caller-supplied GOLEM input. :param image_name: (optional) whether to spawn a docker container with golem :param golem_binary: where golem is installed on the host (or in the docker container) :param output_dir: (optional) where to write the output to :param nproc: nproc :param temporary: whether to delete the working directory afterwards :param workspace_dir: the directory in which golem should be executed (on the host or in the container) :param stream_output: whether golem process should be streamed :return: the simulation results

Source code in core/simulation_components/simulation_packages/golem/golem_run.py 
def run_simulation_golem(
    problem: Union[
        GolemHydrothermalProblemBuilder,
        GolemSimpleReservoirBuilder,
        GolemCustomBuilder,
    ],
    image_name: Optional[str] = None,
    golem_binary: str = "/golem/golem-opt",
    output_dir: Optional[str] = None,
    nproc: int = 4,
    temporary: bool = True,
    workspace_dir: str = "/project",
    stream_output: bool = False,
) -> SimulationResults:
    """
    Build or copy, validate and execute a GOLEM input against a WBGeo mesh.

    If image_name is provided:
    Input and mesh files are copied into a  directory in a named container, results are copied back after the
    run, and the container (including its temporary directory) is removed.

    :param problem: may be an automatically generated hydrothermal/simple-reservoir problem or a ``GolemCustomBuilder`` containing complete caller-supplied GOLEM input.
    :param image_name: (optional) whether to spawn a docker container with golem
    :param golem_binary: where golem is installed on the host (or in the docker container)
    :param output_dir: (optional) where to write the output to
    :param nproc: nproc
    :param temporary: whether to delete the working directory afterwards
    :param workspace_dir: the directory in which golem should be executed (on the host or in the container)
    :param stream_output: whether golem process should be streamed
    :return: the simulation results
    """

    if nproc < 1:
        raise ValueError("nproc must be >= 1")

    create_docker = image_name is not None
    # Call the Docker CLI by its full path. On Windows, gmsh.initialize()
    # overwrites the process PATH with a stale copy (os.environ keeps the
    # right one), so a bare "docker" fails with WinError 2 in any script
    # that meshed with gmsh before running GOLEM.
    docker = shutil.which("docker") if create_docker else None
    if create_docker and docker is None:
        raise RuntimeError("Docker CLI not found, but image_name was given. Install Docker or omit "
                           "image_name to run GOLEM on the host.")
    if not create_docker and shutil.which("mpiexec") is None:
        raise RuntimeError("mpiexec not found on PATH; it is required to run GOLEM on the host. "
                           "Pass image_name to run GOLEM in Docker instead.")

    project = Path(workspace_dir).resolve()
    project.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    output = Path(output_dir).resolve() if output_dir else project / "golem_output"
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)



    if temporary:
        run_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="golem_run_", dir=project))
    else:
        # the directory we work in, shared as a docker volume/copied into the docker
        run_dir = Path(workspace_dir).resolve()
        run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    container_name = f"wbgeo_golem_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}"
    container_created = False
    try:
        input_path = run_dir / "wbgeo.i"
        problem.build_input_file(str(input_path))

        # Stage only explicitly supplied auxiliary GOLEM input files.
        # The directory is copied as `files/` so relative references such as
        # `files/injection_flowrate.csv` resolve from the Docker run directory.
        if isinstance(problem, GolemCustomBuilder) and problem.auxiliary_files_dir:
            source_aux_dir = Path(problem.auxiliary_files_dir).expanduser().resolve()
            if not source_aux_dir.is_dir():
                raise ValueError(
                    "GOLEM auxiliary_files_dir does not exist or is not a directory: "
                    f"{source_aux_dir}"
                )
            target_aux_dir = run_dir / "files"
            shutil.copytree(source_aux_dir, target_aux_dir, dirs_exist_ok=True)
            logger.info("Staged GOLEM auxiliary files: %s -> %s", source_aux_dir, target_aux_dir)
        else:
            target_aux_dir = None

        container_run = "/tmp/wbgeo_golem_run"
        generated = input_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

        # mesh2 consumes hierarchy CSVs produced by mesh1. Convert only the
        # staged copies to PropertyReadFile format and resolve row-count tokens.
        if isinstance(problem, GolemCustomBuilder) and problem.mesh2 is not None and target_aux_dir is not None:
            generated = _prepare_hierarchy_transfer_files(target_aux_dir, generated, stream_output=stream_output)
            input_path.write_text(generated, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")

        external_mesh_mode = False
        if isinstance(problem, GolemCustomBuilder):
            referenced_meshes = problem.referenced_meshes()
            external_mesh = problem.referenced_mesh_file()

            # Hierarchical sampling belongs only to mesh1. mesh2 and mesh_file
            # execute the caller-supplied custom input unchanged.
            if "${GOLEM_MESH1_FILE}" in referenced_meshes:
                generated = problem._inject_hierarchy_samplers(generated)

                if problem.input_file_path:
                    original_input = Path(problem.input_file_path).expanduser().resolve()
                    augmented_input = original_input.with_name(
                        original_input.stem + "_hierarchy_sampling" + original_input.suffix
                    )
                    augmented_input.write_text(generated, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
                    logger.info("Saved hierarchy-augmented GOLEM input: %s", augmented_input)
                input_path.write_text(generated, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
        else:
            referenced_meshes = {"${GOLEM_MESH_FILE}": problem.mesh_results}
            external_mesh = None

        # Paths embedded in wbgeo.i must belong to the namespace where GOLEM
        # actually executes.  Host paths (for example /Users/... on macOS) are
        # not visible inside Docker; the complete staging directory is copied
        # to container_run before the container starts.
        if create_docker:
            execution_run_dir = container_run
        else:
            execution_run_dir = str(run_dir)

        mesh_specs = {
            "${GOLEM_MESH_FILE}": (
                "wbgeo_mesh.exo",
                f"{execution_run_dir}/wbgeo_mesh.exo",
            ),
            "${GOLEM_MESH1_FILE}": (
                "wbgeo_mesh1.exo",
                f"{execution_run_dir}/wbgeo_mesh1.exo",
            ),
            "${GOLEM_MESH2_FILE}": (
                "wbgeo_mesh2.exo",
                f"{execution_run_dir}/wbgeo_mesh2.exo",
            ),
        }
        mesh_paths = {}

        # WBGeo MeshResults modes: export to Exodus exactly as before.
        for placeholder, mesh in referenced_meshes.items():
            filename, container_mesh = mesh_specs[placeholder]
            mesh_path_item = run_dir / filename
            exo = export_mesh_results_to_exodus(mesh, type=exodus_type_for(mesh))
            mesh_path_item.write_bytes(exo.getbuffer())
            mesh_paths[placeholder] = mesh_path_item
            generated = generated.replace(placeholder, container_mesh)

        # External mesh-file mode: copy the existing file; do not re-export it.
        if external_mesh is not None:
            external_mesh_mode = True
            placeholder, source_mesh, requested_name = external_mesh
            staged_name = Path(requested_name).name
            staged_mesh = run_dir / staged_name
            shutil.copy2(source_mesh, staged_mesh)
            container_mesh = f"{execution_run_dir}/{staged_name}"
            mesh_paths[placeholder] = staged_mesh
            generated = generated.replace(placeholder, container_mesh)

        # WBGeo meshes retain the detailed material/block validation. An external
        # mesh has no MeshResults metadata, so validate the input structure and
        # let GOLEM/MOOSE validate block/material compatibility against the file.
        if referenced_meshes:
            validation_mesh = next(iter(referenced_meshes.values()))
            validate_golem_input(
                input_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
                validation_mesh,
                validation_mesh.mesh_type,
            )
        elif external_mesh_mode:
            required_blocks = ["Mesh", "Variables", "Kernels", "Executioner", "Outputs", "BCs", "Materials"]
            missing = [
                block for block in required_blocks
                if not re.search(rf"^\s*\[{re.escape(block)}\]\s*$", generated, re.MULTILINE)
            ]
            if missing:
                raise ValueError("Missing required blocks: " + ", ".join(missing))

        input_path.write_text(generated, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")

        # Legacy variable retained for the rest of the runner and run_info.
        # For hierarchical-only custom inputs it points to mesh1 when present,
        # otherwise mesh2.
        mesh_path = (mesh_paths.get("${GOLEM_MESH_FILE}")
                     or mesh_paths.get("${GOLEM_MESH1_FILE}")
                     or mesh_paths.get("${GOLEM_MESH2_FILE}"))

        logger.debug("GOLEM host staging directory: %s", run_dir)
        logger.debug("Input to copy: %s", input_path)
        logger.debug("Mesh to copy: %s", mesh_path)
        if create_docker:
            logger.debug("Docker container: %s", container_name)
        logger.debug("MPI processes: %d", nproc)

        # Resolve executable and input paths in the namespace where GOLEM runs.
        # Host paths (for example /Users/... on macOS) are not valid inside
        # Docker, because the staged run directory is copied to container_run.
        if create_docker:
            golem_input_path = f"{container_run}/wbgeo.i"
        else:
            golem_input_path = str(input_path)

        golem_command = ["mpiexec", "-n", str(nproc), "--allow-run-as-root"]
        golem_command.extend([str(golem_binary), "-i", golem_input_path])

        if create_docker:  # run via docker create/run
            docker_command = (
                #f'export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="{golem_library_path}:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH"; ' # todo: check if still required?
                f'set -e; mkdir -p "{container_run}/output"; '
                f'cd "{container_run}"; '
                f'{shlex.join(golem_command)}'
            )
            create_command = [
                docker, "create", "--name", container_name, "-i",
                # workspace_dir is a host path (it may be relative or a Windows
                # path, which Docker rejects as a mount target). GOLEM runs in
                # container_run, filled by docker cp below, so the workspace
                # is mounted at a fixed container path.
                "-v", f"{project}:{CONTAINER_WORKSPACE}",
                image_name,
                "-c", docker_command,
            ]
            created = subprocess.run(
                create_command, text=True, capture_output=True, check=False
            )
            if created.returncode:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    "Could not create the GOLEM Docker container:\n"
                    + created.stdout + created.stderr
                )
            container_created = True

            # Copy the complete staging directory so the input and mesh exist in
            # the container independently of the host bind mount.
            copied = subprocess.run(
                [docker, "cp", str(run_dir) + "/.",
                 f"{container_name}:{container_run}"],
                text=True, capture_output=True, check=False,
            )
            if copied.returncode:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    "Could not copy GOLEM input files into the container:\n"
                    + copied.stdout + copied.stderr
                )

            transcript = _stream_process([docker, "start", "-a", container_name], stream_output=stream_output)

            # Copy the ENTIRE GOLEM working directory back from the container.
            # Some MOOSE outputs (especially CSV when no file_base is given) are
            # written directly beside wbgeo.i rather than inside output/.
            container_snapshot = run_dir / "container_run"
            container_snapshot.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

            copied_back = subprocess.run(
                [docker, "cp", f"{container_name}:{container_run}/.",
                 str(container_snapshot)],
                text=True, capture_output=True, check=False,
            )
            if copied_back.returncode:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    "GOLEM completed but its working directory could not be copied "
                    "from Docker:\n" + copied_back.stdout + copied_back.stderr
                )

            # First preserve everything explicitly written under output/ at the
            # root of the caller's output_dir.
            staged_output = container_snapshot / "output"
            if staged_output.is_dir():
                shutil.copytree(staged_output, output, dirs_exist_ok=True)

            # Then preserve generated files/directories written directly in the
            # GOLEM working directory. Do not re-copy the staged input/mesh or the
            # output directory itself; those inputs are saved below with stable
            # WBGeo names.
            excluded_root_names = {
                "wbgeo.i", "wbgeo_mesh.exo", "wbgeo_mesh1.exo", "wbgeo_mesh2.exo", "output"
            }
            excluded_root_names.update(path.name for path in mesh_paths.values())
            for item in container_snapshot.iterdir():
                if item.name in excluded_root_names:
                    continue
                destination = output / item.name
                if item.is_dir():
                    shutil.copytree(item, destination, dirs_exist_ok=True)
                elif item.is_file():
                    shutil.copy2(item, destination)

            # The Docker working directory has now been fully copied into the
            # caller's output directory (with checkpoint directories preserved
            # for custom inputs). Remove the temporary host-side snapshot immediately
            # instead of keeping a duplicate until the end of the run.
            shutil.rmtree(container_snapshot, ignore_errors=True)

            copied_files = sorted(
                (path for path in output.rglob("*") if path.is_file()),
                key=lambda path: str(path),
            )
            logger.info("Copied %d GOLEM output file(s) to %s", len(copied_files), output)
            for path in copied_files:
                logger.debug("  %s", path.relative_to(output))
        else:
            # if golem is installed locally: Run the golem command directly
            if stream_output:
                transcript = _stream_process(golem_command, cwd=run_dir, stream_output=True)
            else:
                res = subprocess.run(golem_command, cwd=run_dir, capture_output=True, text=True)
                if res.returncode != 0:
                    raise RuntimeError(
                        f"GOLEM execution failed (exit code {res.returncode}).\n"
                        f"Command: {shlex.join(golem_command)}\n"
                        f"Working directory: {run_dir}\n"
                        f"stdout:\n{res.stdout or '(empty)'}\n"
                        f"stderr:\n{res.stderr or '(empty)'}"
                    )
                transcript = res.stdout
            # Direct and shared-workspace executions write to run_dir. Copy
            # outputs to output_dir so result loading works in every mode.
            if (run_dir / "output").is_dir() and (run_dir / "output").resolve() != output:
                shutil.copytree(run_dir / "output", output, dirs_exist_ok=True)
            excluded = {"wbgeo.i", "wbgeo_mesh.exo", "wbgeo_mesh1.exo", "wbgeo_mesh2.exo", "output"}
            excluded.update(path.name for path in mesh_paths.values())
            for item in run_dir.iterdir():
                if item.name in excluded or item.resolve() == output:
                    continue
                target = output / item.name
                if item.is_dir():
                    shutil.copytree(item, target, dirs_exist_ok=True)
                elif item.is_file():
                    shutil.copy2(item, target)
            copied_files = sorted(path for path in output.rglob("*") if path.is_file())

        # Automatically generated WBGeo problems do not need GOLEM/MOOSE
        # recovery directories in their returned results. Custom GOLEM
        # inputs may intentionally request checkpoints for restart, so
        # preserve those directories for GolemCustomBuilder runs.
        if not isinstance(problem, GolemCustomBuilder):
            checkpoint_dirs = sorted(
                (
                    path
                    for path in output.rglob("*")
                    if path.is_dir() and path.name.endswith("_cp")
                ),
                key=lambda path: len(path.parts),
                reverse=True,
            )
            for checkpoint_dir in checkpoint_dirs:
                shutil.rmtree(checkpoint_dir, ignore_errors=True)


        # Hierarchy samplers execute at TIMESTEP_END so their vectors are
        # populated before CSV output.  MOOSE writes one CSV per timestep
        # (for example hierarchy_inside_0000.csv, ..._0001.csv).  Keep only
        # the highest timestep for each hierarchy sampling group so the final
        # WBGeo output directory contains the last solved state only.
        hierarchy_csv_re = re.compile(
            r"^(?P<prefix>.*hierarchy_(?P<group>.+))_(?P<step>\d+)\.csv$"
        )
        hierarchy_csv_groups = {}
        for csv_path in output.rglob("*.csv"):
            match = hierarchy_csv_re.match(csv_path.name)
            if match:
                key = (csv_path.parent, match.group("prefix"))
                hierarchy_csv_groups.setdefault(key, []).append( (int(match.group("step")), csv_path) )

        for entries in hierarchy_csv_groups.values():
            last_step = max(step for step, _ in entries)
            for step, csv_path in entries:
                if step != last_step:
                    csv_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)

        # Organize final hierarchy sampler CSVs exactly like the hierarchy BC
        # coordinate outputs: big_frame contains the coordinates sampled
        # directly by GOLEM on mesh1, while small_frame contains the same rows
        # and solution values with only x/y/z transformed into mesh2's final
        # coordinate frame.  The affine matrix is generated by
        # hierarchical_mesh(), so no transformation is estimated from CSVs.
        if isinstance(problem, GolemCustomBuilder) and problem.hierarchy_sample_nodes:
            transform_meta = problem.hierarchy_sample_nodes.get(
                "transformation_parameters", {}
            )
            matrix_data = transform_meta.get("big_to_small_matrix")
            if matrix_data is not None:
                big_to_small = np.asarray(matrix_data, dtype=float)
                if big_to_small.shape != (4, 4):
                    raise ValueError(
                        "hierarchy transformation big_to_small_matrix must be 4x4"
                    )

                final_hierarchy_csvs = [
                    path for path in output.rglob("*.csv")
                    if "hierarchy_" in path.name
                    and path.parent.name not in {"big_frame", "small_frame"}
                ]
                if final_hierarchy_csvs:
                    big_dir = output / "big_frame"
                    small_dir = output / "small_frame"
                    big_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                    small_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

                for source_csv in final_hierarchy_csvs:
                    name_match = hierarchy_csv_re.match(source_csv.name)
                    if name_match is None:
                        continue
                    group = name_match.group("group")
                    stable_name = f"hierarchy_{group}.csv"
                    big_csv = big_dir / stable_name
                    small_csv = small_dir / stable_name

                    # Convert the raw PointValueSampler CSV to a transfer-file
                    # format that is independent of whether the outer problem is
                    # TH, THM, or samples any other variables.  Coordinates are
                    # always written first; all sampled solution variables are
                    # retained in their original order.  PointValueSampler
                    # bookkeeping columns (time/id) are intentionally omitted.
                    with source_csv.open("r", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as src:
                        reader = csv.DictReader(src)
                        raw_fieldnames = reader.fieldnames or []
                        coordinate_names = None
                        for candidate in (("x", "y", "z"), ("X", "Y", "Z")):
                            if all(name in raw_fieldnames for name in candidate):
                                coordinate_names = candidate
                                break
                        if coordinate_names is None:
                            raise ValueError(
                                f"Hierarchy sampler CSV {source_csv.name!r} has no "
                                "x/y/z coordinate columns."
                            )
                        rows = list(reader)

                    x_name, y_name, z_name = coordinate_names
                    metadata_names = {"time", "id", x_name, y_name, z_name}
                    variable_names = [
                        name for name in raw_fieldnames
                        if name not in metadata_names
                    ]
                    transfer_fieldnames = ["x", "y", "z", *variable_names]

                    # Write the big-frame transfer CSV in the same clean format.
                    with big_csv.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as dst:
                        writer = csv.DictWriter(dst, fieldnames=transfer_fieldnames)
                        writer.writeheader()
                        for row in rows:
                            writer.writerow({
                                "x": row[x_name],
                                "y": row[y_name],
                                "z": row[z_name],
                                **{name: row[name] for name in variable_names},
                            })

                    # Write the corresponding small-frame CSV.  Only coordinates
                    # are transformed; every sampled TH/THM variable is copied
                    # unchanged.
                    with small_csv.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as dst:
                        writer = csv.DictWriter(dst, fieldnames=transfer_fieldnames)
                        writer.writeheader()
                        for row in rows:
                            point = np.array([
                                float(row[x_name]),
                                float(row[y_name]),
                                float(row[z_name]),
                                1.0,
                            ])
                            transformed = big_to_small @ point
                            writer.writerow({
                                "x": f"{transformed[0]:.17g}",
                                "y": f"{transformed[1]:.17g}",
                                "z": f"{transformed[2]:.17g}",
                                **{name: row[name] for name in variable_names},
                            })

                    source_csv.unlink(missing_ok=True)


        # Exodus is still required to load the numerical result into WBGeo,
        # but the search below does not restrict which files are preserved.
        candidates = list(output.rglob("*.e")) + list(output.rglob("*.exo"))
        if not candidates:
            copied_listing = "\n".join(
                f"  {path.relative_to(output)}" for path in copied_files
            ) or "  <none>"
            raise RuntimeError(
                "GOLEM completed and its output files were copied, but no "
                f"Exodus result exists in {output}. Copied files:\n"
                + copied_listing
            )
        result_file = max(candidates, key=lambda path: path.stat().st_mtime)

        transcript_path = output / "golem_stdout.txt"
        transcript_path.write_text(transcript, encoding="utf-8")
        if temporary:
            # Preserve the generated inputs beside results before cleanup.
            saved_input = output / "wbgeo_generated.i"
            shutil.copy2(input_path, saved_input)
            saved_mesh_paths = {}
            for placeholder, source_path in mesh_paths.items():
                destination = output / source_path.name
                shutil.copy2(source_path, destination)
                saved_mesh_paths[placeholder] = destination
            saved_mesh = (saved_mesh_paths.get("${GOLEM_MESH_FILE}")
                          or saved_mesh_paths.get("${GOLEM_MESH1_FILE}")
                          or saved_mesh_paths.get("${GOLEM_MESH2_FILE}"))
        else:
            saved_input = input_path
            saved_mesh_paths = dict(mesh_paths)
            saved_mesh = mesh_path

        run_info = {
            "input_file": str(saved_input),
            "mesh_file": str(saved_mesh),
            "mesh1_file": str(saved_mesh_paths["${GOLEM_MESH1_FILE}"]) if "${GOLEM_MESH1_FILE}" in saved_mesh_paths else None,
            "mesh2_file": str(saved_mesh_paths["${GOLEM_MESH2_FILE}"]) if "${GOLEM_MESH2_FILE}" in saved_mesh_paths else None,
            "output_file": str(result_file),
            "output_dir": str(output),
            "stdout_file": str(transcript_path),
        }
        logger.debug("GOLEM Exodus result: %s", result_file)
        logger.debug("Loading GOLEM Exodus result into SimulationResults...")
        simulation_results = load_exodus_results(run_info)
        # Make the result self-contained, so nothing has to stay on disk:
        # the fields are already loaded; add GOLEM's CSV output as tables,
        # the input that ran, its console output and block names.
        simulation_results.solver = "golem"
        simulation_results.solver_output = {"golem": transcript}
        simulation_results.input_files = {"wbgeo.i": input_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")}
        simulation_results.solver_tables = _read_solver_tables(output)
        simulation_results.block_names = {
            **_builder_block_names(problem), **simulation_results.block_names,
        }
        if not simulation_results.nodes_by_time:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"The GOLEM Exodus file at {result_file} contained no readable time steps."
            )
        logger.info("Loaded %d GOLEM time step(s).", len(simulation_results.nodes_by_time))
        return simulation_results
    finally:
        if container_created:
            removed = subprocess.run(
                [docker, "rm", "-f", container_name],
                text=True, capture_output=True, check=False,
            )
            if removed.returncode:
                logger.warning(
                    "Could not remove temporary GOLEM container %s: %s",
                    container_name,
                    (removed.stdout + removed.stderr).strip(),
                )
        if temporary:
            shutil.rmtree(run_dir, ignore_errors=True)

docs.title: validate_golem_input(content, mesh_results, mesh_type)
docs.text:
Validate a GOLEM/MOOSE input before starting Docker.

This mirrors the structural checks used by simulation_run while accepting both modern [name] and legacy [./name] MOOSE subsection syntax, which is emitted by the GOLEM builders in this module family.

Source code in core/simulation_components/simulation_packages/golem/golem_run.py 
def validate_golem_input(content: str, mesh_results, mesh_type: MeshType) -> None:
    """Validate a GOLEM/MOOSE input before starting Docker.

    This mirrors the structural checks used by ``simulation_run`` while
    accepting both modern ``[name]`` and legacy ``[./name]`` MOOSE subsection
    syntax, which is emitted by the GOLEM builders in this module family.
    """
    required_blocks = [
        "Mesh",
        "Variables",
        "Kernels",
        "Executioner",
        "Outputs",
        "BCs",
        "Materials",
    ]
    _, parsed_blocks = locate_blocks(content)
    present_top_level = {block.name for block in parsed_blocks if block.depth == 0}
    missing = [block for block in required_blocks if block not in present_top_level]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError("Missing required blocks: " + ", ".join(missing))

    mesh_pattern = re.compile(
        r"""
        ^\s*\[Mesh\]\s*$
        .*?
        ^\s*type\s*=\s*FileMeshGenerator\s*$
        .*?
        ^\s*file\s*=\s*\$\{GOLEM_MESH(?:1|2)?_FILE\}\s*$
        """,
        re.DOTALL | re.MULTILINE | re.VERBOSE,
    )
    if not mesh_pattern.search(content):
        raise ValueError(
            "Mesh block must contain type = FileMeshGenerator and "
            "file = ${GOLEM_MESH_FILE}, ${GOLEM_MESH1_FILE}, or ${GOLEM_MESH2_FILE}"
        )

    # Shared block locator handles nested modern/legacy syntax, comments and
    # quoted values consistently with hierarchy-sampler insertion.
    extract_parent_block = block_body
    get_direct_child_blocks = direct_children

    materials_content = extract_parent_block(content, "Materials")
    if not materials_content.strip():
        raise ValueError("Materials block is empty")

    material_sections = get_direct_child_blocks(content, "Materials")
    if not material_sections:
        raise ValueError("No material definitions found inside the [Materials] block")

    if mesh_type == MeshType.UNSTRUCTURED:
        n_mesh_blocks = len(mesh_results.elements) - 6
    else:
        n_mesh_blocks = len(mesh_results.elements)

    if n_mesh_blocks <= 0:
        raise ValueError("The mesh has no exportable material blocks")

    # A material section does not have to correspond one-to-one with a mesh
    # block.  GolemSimpleReservoirBuilder intentionally groups several
    # mesh blocks into sections such as [uniform_rock], [fractures], and [well].
    # Validate the actual block assignments instead of counting subsections.
    # Material assignments may use either numeric Exodus block IDs or names
    # introduced by a MOOSE RenameBlockGenerator.  Resolve renamed blocks back
    # to their original numeric Exodus IDs so the coverage check below remains
    # valid for both forms.
    rename_name_to_id = {}
    rename_sections = re.finditer(
        r"type\s*=\s*RenameBlockGenerator(?P<body>.*?)(?=^\s*\[\]\s*$)",
        content,
        re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL,
    )
    for section in rename_sections:
        body = section.group("body")
        old_match = re.search(
            r"old_block\s*=\s*(['\"])(.*?)\1", body, re.DOTALL
        )
        new_match = re.search(
            r"new_block\s*=\s*(['\"])(.*?)\1", body, re.DOTALL
        )
        if not old_match or not new_match:
            continue
        old_tokens = old_match.group(2).split()
        new_tokens = new_match.group(2).split()
        if len(old_tokens) != len(new_tokens):
            raise ValueError(
                "RenameBlockGenerator must contain the same number of "
                f"old_block and new_block entries ({len(old_tokens)} != "
                f"{len(new_tokens)})"
            )
        for old_token, new_name in zip(old_tokens, new_tokens):
            try:
                old_id = int(old_token)
            except ValueError as exc:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Invalid old_block id {old_token!r} in RenameBlockGenerator"
                ) from exc
            if new_name in rename_name_to_id and rename_name_to_id[new_name] != old_id:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"RenameBlockGenerator assigns duplicate new block name "
                    f"{new_name!r} to multiple block IDs"
                )
            rename_name_to_id[new_name] = old_id

    material_block_ids = set()
    for match in re.finditer(
        r"^\s*block\s*=\s*['\"]?([^'\"#\n]+)['\"]?\s*(?:#.*)?$",
        materials_content,
        re.MULTILINE,
    ):
        for token in match.group(1).split():
            try:
                material_block_ids.add(int(token))
            except ValueError:
                if token not in rename_name_to_id:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Unknown material block name {token!r} in [Materials]; "
                        "it is neither a numeric Exodus block ID nor a name "
                        "defined by RenameBlockGenerator"
                    )
                material_block_ids.add(rename_name_to_id[token])

    if not material_block_ids:
        raise ValueError(
            "No material 'block = ...' assignments found inside [Materials]"
        )

    expected_block_ids = set(range(1, n_mesh_blocks + 1))
    missing_material_ids = sorted(expected_block_ids - material_block_ids)
    extra_material_ids = sorted(material_block_ids - expected_block_ids)

    if missing_material_ids:
        raise ValueError(
            "The following mesh blocks have no material assignment: "
            + ", ".join(map(str, missing_material_ids))
        )
    if extra_material_ids:
        raise ValueError(
            "The [Materials] block references non-exportable mesh block ids: "
            + ", ".join(map(str, extra_material_ids))
        )

    variable_names = get_direct_child_blocks(content, "Variables")
    if not variable_names:
        raise ValueError("No variables found inside the [Variables] block")

    kernels_content = extract_parent_block(content, "Kernels")
    if not kernels_content.strip():
        raise ValueError("Kernels block is empty")

    kernel_variables = set(
        re.findall(
            r"^\s*variable\s*=\s*['\"]?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)['\"]?\s*$",
            kernels_content,
            re.MULTILINE,
        )
    )
    variables_without_kernel = [
        variable for variable in variable_names if variable not in kernel_variables
    ]
    if variables_without_kernel:
        raise ValueError(
            "The following variables do not have at least one kernel: "
            + ", ".join(variables_without_kernel)
        )

    logger.info(
        "GOLEM input validation successful: %d mesh blocks covered by %d material sections; variables=%s",
        n_mesh_blocks,
        len(material_sections),
        ", ".join(variable_names),
    )

docs.text:
Literal material coefficients of a custom SfePy file, per mesh group.

group_values: SfePy group id (cells of group N) -> coefficient -> value. conflicts: (group id, coefficient) pairs that two materials linked to the same group define with different values; left out of group_values. unlinked: coefficients defined in materials whose material is not linked to any cells of group N region through equations.

Source code in core/simulation_components/simulation_packages/sfepy/sfepy_input_parser.py 
@dataclass
class CustomSfepyMaterials:
    """Literal material coefficients of a custom SfePy file, per mesh group.

    group_values: SfePy group id (``cells of group N``) -> coefficient -> value.
    conflicts: (group id, coefficient) pairs that two materials linked to the
        same group define with different values; left out of group_values.
    unlinked: coefficients defined in ``materials`` whose material is not
        linked to any ``cells of group N`` region through ``equations``.
    """
    group_values: Dict[int, Dict[str, float]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    conflicts: Set[Tuple[int, str]] = field(default_factory=set)
    unlinked: Set[str] = field(default_factory=set)

Read the literal coefficients a custom SfePy file assigns to each mesh group.

Only direct numeric constants in the module-level materials mapping are read (arithmetic of literals and of module-level scalar constants is allowed). A material is linked to a group through any equation term dw_*.<integral>.<region>(<material>.<coefficient>, ...) whose region is cells of group N; the coefficient used in the equation does not need to be the one read, so metadata such as porosity is picked up too.

Source code in core/simulation_components/simulation_packages/sfepy/sfepy_input_parser.py 
def custom_sfepy_group_properties(content: str) -> CustomSfepyMaterials:
    """Read the literal coefficients a custom SfePy file assigns to each mesh group.

    Only direct numeric constants in the module-level ``materials`` mapping
    are read (arithmetic of literals and of module-level scalar constants is
    allowed). A material is linked to a group through any equation term
    ``dw_*.<integral>.<region>(<material>.<coefficient>, ...)`` whose region
    is ``cells of group N``; the coefficient used in the equation does not
    need to be the one read, so metadata such as porosity is picked up too.
    """
    tree = ast.parse(content)
    material_defs: Dict[str, Dict[str, float]] = {}
    region_groups: Dict[str, int] = {}
    equations = {}
    constants: Dict[str, float] = {}

    def scalar(node):
        """Evaluate only arithmetic of numeric literals and known scalar constants."""
        if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and type(node.value) in (int, float):
            return float(node.value)
        if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and node.id in constants:
            return constants[node.id]
        if isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp) and isinstance(node.op, (ast.USub, ast.UAdd)):
            v = scalar(node.operand)
            return -v if isinstance(node.op, ast.USub) else v
        if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp) and isinstance(node.op, (ast.Add, ast.Sub, ast.Mult, ast.Div, ast.Pow)):
            a, b = scalar(node.left), scalar(node.right)
            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Add):
                return a + b
            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Sub):
                return a - b
            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Mult):
                return a * b
            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Div):
                return a / b
            return a ** b
        raise ValueError("not a static scalar")

    for node in tree.body:
        if not isinstance(node, (ast.Assign, ast.AnnAssign)):
            continue
        targets = node.targets if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) else [node.target]
        value = node.value
        for target in targets:
            if not isinstance(target, ast.Name):
                continue
            name = target.id
            if name not in ("materials", "regions", "equations"):
                try:
                    result = scalar(value)
                    if np.isfinite(result):
                        constants[name] = result
                except (ValueError, TypeError, ZeroDivisionError, OverflowError):
                    pass
            if name == "materials" and isinstance(value, ast.Dict):
                # Parse material entries independently: a single expression or
                # callback must not make the entire dictionary unreadable.
                material_defs = {}
                for key, definition in zip(value.keys, value.values):
                    try:
                        mat_name = ast.literal_eval(key)
                    except (ValueError, TypeError, SyntaxError, MemoryError):
                        continue
                    if not isinstance(definition, (ast.Tuple, ast.List)) or not definition.elts:
                        continue
                    fields_node = definition.elts[0]
                    if not isinstance(fields_node, ast.Dict):
                        continue
                    fields = {}
                    for field_key, field_value in zip(fields_node.keys, fields_node.values):
                        try:
                            field_name = ast.literal_eval(field_key)
                            number = scalar(field_value)
                            if np.isfinite(number):
                                fields[field_name] = number
                        except (ValueError, TypeError, SyntaxError, MemoryError,
                                ZeroDivisionError, OverflowError):
                            continue
                    material_defs[mat_name] = fields
            elif name == "regions" and isinstance(value, ast.Dict):
                for key_node, definition_node in zip(value.keys, value.values):
                    try:
                        region_name = ast.literal_eval(key_node)
                        selector_node = (definition_node.elts[0]
                                         if isinstance(definition_node, (ast.Tuple, ast.List))
                                         and definition_node.elts else definition_node)
                        selector = ast.literal_eval(selector_node)
                    except (ValueError, TypeError, SyntaxError, MemoryError):
                        continue
                    match = re.fullmatch(r"cells of group\s+(\d+)", str(selector).strip())
                    if match:
                        region_groups[region_name] = int(match.group(1))
            elif name == "equations":
                try:
                    equations = ast.literal_eval(value)
                except (ValueError, TypeError, SyntaxError, MemoryError):
                    pass

    material_groups: Dict[str, Set[int]] = {}
    for equation in equations.values():
        if not isinstance(equation, str):
            continue
        # term.integral.region(material.coefficient, ...), also across line breaks.
        for region, material in re.findall(r"\b(?:dw_\w+|ev_\w+)\.\w+\.(\w+)\s*\(\s*(\w+)\.\w+", equation):
            if region in region_groups and material in material_defs:
                material_groups.setdefault(material, set()).add(region_groups[region])

    result = CustomSfepyMaterials()
    for material, fields in material_defs.items():
        if material not in material_groups:
            result.unlinked.update(fields)
            continue
        for group_id in material_groups[material]:
            values = result.group_values.setdefault(group_id, {})
            for coefficient, value in fields.items():
                if (group_id, coefficient) in result.conflicts:
                    continue
                if coefficient in values and values[coefficient] != value:
                    del values[coefficient]
                    result.conflicts.add((group_id, coefficient))
                    continue
                values[coefficient] = value
    linked = {c for values in result.group_values.values() for c in values}
    result.unlinked -= linked | {c for _, c in result.conflicts}
    return result

docs.title: Sfepy model builder
docs.text:
Auto-generates SfePy input file(s) for a simplified, single-phase Darcy flow + advective-conductive heat transport problem, inferring rock units and boundary regions directly from a WBGeo MeshResults + StructuralModelResults pair, instead of a hand-written static file with hardcoded regions.

This is the input-data side only: SfepyHydrothermalProblemBuilder builds the generated SfePy input files and their configuration. Actually running them (subprocess launch, output loading) lives in sfepy_run.py, split out to keep "build the input data" and "run the simulation" as separate concerns -- matching the Workbench's component/connector model, where SfepyHydrothermalProblemBuilder is the input-data-generator component and run_simulation_sfepy() (sfepy_run.py) is the run component.

Solved as two sequential, single-physics stages (pressure, then temperature), not one monolithic multi-field system -- see run_simulation_sfepy()'s docstring for why: solving both together in one combined linear system was tried first and turned out to be badly conditioned (pressure ~1e6 Pa and temperature ~10s of degC in the same matrix), and no amount of preconditioner tuning fixed it. Segregating matches the actual physics anyway: temperature depends on the flow field, but pressure never depends on temperature in this model.

Wired up as Workbench components in simulation_workbench_components.py (build_hydrothermal_problem, run_simulation, export_simulation_results), including a SmartInput sidebar for per-rock-unit, fluid, and fault-zone property editing (matching structural_workbench_components.py's interpolation-options pattern). build_hydrothermal_problem wraps its SfepyHydrothermalProblemBuilder in a shared SfepyProblem envelope (also defined in this file) so it and build_custom_sfepy_problem's SfepyCustomBuilder output register as the same Workbench type -- run_simulation is one component accepting either, rather than two separate Run components.

class FluidProperties(BaseModel):
    """Canonical fluid properties shared by the SfePy and GOLEM builders."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)

    mu: float = Field(
        1.0e-3, validation_alias=AliasChoices("mu", "viscosity")
    )
    k_fluid: float = Field(
        0.6,
        validation_alias=AliasChoices("k_fluid", "thermal_conductivity"),
    )
    density: float = 1000.0                   # kg/m^3
    heat_capacity: Optional[float] = None     # J/(kg*K)
    rho_c_fluid: Optional[float] = None       # J/(m^3*K)
    fluid_modulus: float = 2.2e9              # Pa

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def calculate_volumetric_heat_capacity(self) -> "FluidProperties":
        if self.mu <= 0 or self.k_fluid <= 0 or self.density <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                "fluid viscosity, thermal conductivity and density must be > 0"
            )
        if self.heat_capacity is None and self.rho_c_fluid is None:
            self.rho_c_fluid = 4.186e6
            self.heat_capacity = self.rho_c_fluid / self.density
        elif self.heat_capacity is None:
            self.heat_capacity = float(self.rho_c_fluid) / self.density
        elif self.rho_c_fluid is None:
            self.rho_c_fluid = self.density * self.heat_capacity
        elif not np.isclose(
            self.rho_c_fluid,
            self.density * self.heat_capacity,
            rtol=1.0e-10,
            atol=0.0,
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "rho_c_fluid must equal density * heat_capacity"
            )
        if self.heat_capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError("fluid heat_capacity must be > 0")
        return self

    @property
    def viscosity(self) -> float:
        return self.mu

    @property
    def thermal_conductivity(self) -> float:
        return self.k_fluid

class RockUnitProperties(BaseModel):
    """Canonical rock properties shared by the SfePy and GOLEM builders."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)

    name: str
    porosity: float = 0.15
    permeability: float = 1e-14   # isotropic scalar permeability, m^2
    k_solid: float = Field(
        2.5,
        validation_alias=AliasChoices("k_solid", "thermal_conductivity"),
    )
    density: float = 2600.0                   # kg/m^3
    heat_capacity: Optional[float] = None     # J/(kg*K)
    rho_c_solid: Optional[float] = None       # J/(m^3*K)
    fluid_modulus: float = 2.2e9              # Pa, used by GOLEM

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def calculate_volumetric_heat_capacity(self) -> "RockUnitProperties":
        if not 0.0 <= self.porosity <= 1.0:
            raise ValueError(f"porosity for {self.name!r} must be in [0, 1]")
        if self.permeability <= 0 or self.k_solid <= 0 or self.density <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"permeability, thermal conductivity and density for "
                f"{self.name!r} must be > 0"
            )
        if self.heat_capacity is None and self.rho_c_solid is None:
            self.rho_c_solid = 2.2e6
            self.heat_capacity = self.rho_c_solid / self.density
        elif self.heat_capacity is None:
            self.heat_capacity = float(self.rho_c_solid) / self.density
        elif self.rho_c_solid is None:
            self.rho_c_solid = self.density * self.heat_capacity
        elif not np.isclose(
            self.rho_c_solid,
            self.density * self.heat_capacity,
            rtol=1.0e-10,
            atol=0.0,
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                f"rho_c_solid for {self.name!r} must equal density * "
                "heat_capacity"
            )
        if self.heat_capacity <= 0 or self.fluid_modulus <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"heat_capacity and fluid_modulus for {self.name!r} must be > 0"
            )
        return self

    @property
    def thermal_conductivity(self) -> float:
        return self.k_solid

    def effective_conductivity(self, fluid: FluidProperties) -> float:
        """Porosity-weighted thermal conductivity of the saturated rock (solid + pore fluid)."""
        return self.porosity * fluid.k_fluid + (1 - self.porosity) * self.k_solid

    def effective_heat_capacity(self, fluid: FluidProperties) -> float:
        """Porosity-weighted volumetric heat capacity of the saturated rock (solid + pore fluid)."""
        return self.porosity * fluid.rho_c_fluid + (1 - self.porosity) * self.rho_c_solid

docs.title: SfepyCustomBuilder
docs.text:
Wraps a user-supplied, already-complete SfePy input file (with its own internal staging/sequencing logic -- e.g. a hand-written GOLEM-style coupled problem) instead of auto-generating one like SfepyHydrothermalProblemBuilder does. Runs through the same run_simulation_sfepy() and returns the same SimulationResults type.

input_file_contents is stored as text, not a file path: @wbgeo_type instances are serialized/reconstructed between separate Workbench component executions, and a temp file path would not survive that round trip. The content is only written to disk transiently at run time, matching how SfepyHydrothermalProblemBuilder's own generated input files work.

Validated at construction against mesh_results (known mesh type, known lithology mapping, and a best-effort static check that every 'cells of group N' the file references actually exists on the mesh -- see check_custom_sfepy_regions). This validation is deliberately not exhaustive: it cannot catch wrong material properties or malformed equations, only structural mismatches with the mesh. sfepy-run's own region resolution remains the final authority at run time.

Unlike SfepyHydrothermalProblemBuilder, no pressure/heat staging, no velocity handoff -- the file is assumed to already contain everything it needs and gets run in a single sfepy-run invocation (see run_simulation_sfepy in sfepy_run.py). On an unstructured mesh, the same mesh_type_code == "unstr" pre-filter SfepyHydrothermalProblemBuilder relies on (_run_sfepy_input_file, dropping non-volume blocks before Exodus export) applies here too -- so a custom file cannot reference a non-volume (fault-surface/boundary) block by group number on an unstructured mesh, the same limitation SfepyHydrothermalProblemBuilder already has. mesh_results with any well/source (dim < 2) block is rejected outright at construction (see check_mesh_has_no_engineering_objects) -- not supported yet.

fault_zone_n_voxels: optional opt-in for a "damage zone" cell selection, the same mechanism SfepyHydrothermalProblemBuilder uses (see compute_fault_zone_cell_mask) -- a band of cells straddling each active fault's trace gets reassigned its own group id (self.fault_group_id), referenceable from the custom file as 'cells of group {fault_group_id}' (e.g. as its own 'Omega_fault' region). Unlike SfepyHydrothermalProblemBuilder, no material/equation is auto-generated for this group -- the custom file's author decides what to do with it; this only provides the cell selection. Requires geomodel_result (raises if not given). None (default) leaves the mesh's real lithology groups as the only ones available, exactly like today.

    round trip. The content is only written to disk transiently at run
    time, matching how SfepyHydrothermalProblemBuilder's own generated input
    files work.

    Validated at construction against mesh_results (known mesh type,
    known lithology mapping, and a best-effort static check that every

    velocity handoff -- the file is assumed to already contain everything
    it needs and gets run in a single sfepy-run invocation (see
    run_simulation_sfepy in sfepy_run.py). On an unstructured
    mesh, the same mesh_type_code == "unstr" pre-filter
    SfepyHydrothermalProblemBuilder relies on (_run_sfepy_input_file, dropping
    non-volume blocks before Exodus export) applies here too -- so a
    custom file cannot reference a non-volume (fault-surface/boundary)
    block by group number on an unstructured mesh, the same limitation
    SfepyHydrothermalProblemBuilder already has. mesh_results with any
    well/source (dim < 2) block is rejected outright at construction (see
    check_mesh_has_no_engineering_objects) -- not supported yet.

    fault_zone_n_voxels: optional opt-in for a "damage zone" cell
    selection, the same mechanism SfepyHydrothermalProblemBuilder uses (see
    compute_fault_zone_cell_mask) -- a band of cells straddling each
    active fault's trace gets reassigned its own group id
    (self.fault_group_id), referenceable from the custom file as
    'cells of group {fault_group_id}' (e.g. as its own 'Omega_fault'
    region). Unlike SfepyHydrothermalProblemBuilder, no material/equation is
    auto-generated for this group -- the custom file's author decides
    what to do with it; this only provides the cell selection. Requires
    geomodel_result (raises if not given). None (default) leaves the
    mesh's real lithology groups as the only ones available, exactly like
    today.
    """
    input_file_contents: str
    mesh_results: MeshResults
    geomodel_result: Optional[StructuralModelResults] = None
    fault_zone_n_voxels: Optional[int] = None
    print_linear_residuals: bool = False

    def __post_init__(self):
        check_mesh_has_known_type(self.mesh_results)
        check_mesh_has_no_engineering_objects(self.mesh_results)
        check_mesh_has_lithology_mapping(self.mesh_results)
        self.mesh_type = self.mesh_results.mesh_type
        self.mat_id_to_lithology = map_mat_id_to_lithology(self.mesh_results)

        self.fault_zone_cell_mask: Optional[np.ndarray] = None
        self.fault_group_id: Optional[int] = None
        if self.fault_zone_n_voxels is not None:
            if self.geomodel_result is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    "fault_zone_n_voxels was given but geomodel_result is None -- "
                    "computing the fault-zone cell mask needs the structural model."
                )
            self.fault_zone_cell_mask = compute_fault_zone_cell_mask(
                self.mesh_results, self.geomodel_result, self.fault_zone_n_voxels,
            )
            if self.fault_zone_cell_mask is not None:
                self.fault_group_id = len(self.mesh_results.elements)

        check_custom_sfepy_regions(
            self.input_file_contents, self.mesh_results,
            extra_valid_groups={self.fault_group_id} if self.fault_group_id is not None else set(),
        )
        if self.geomodel_result is not None:
            n_referenced = len(extract_referenced_groups(self.input_file_contents))
            n_lithologies = len(enumerate_rock_units(self.geomodel_result))
            if n_referenced < n_lithologies:
                logger.warning(
                    "File references %d group(s) via 'cells of group N' but the "
                    "structural model defines %d lithologies -- expected if a "
                    "lithology is split across disconnected mesh blocks (e.g. a "
                    "fault), otherwise the file may be missing coverage.",
                    n_referenced, n_lithologies,
                )

docs.title: SfepyHydrothermalProblemBuilder
docs.text:
Builds SfePy problem-description files for a coupled Darcy flow + heat transport problem, solved as two sequential single-physics stages. Material regions and boundary regions are inferred automatically from the mesh and structural model.

The default linear_solver="petsc" requires petsc4py and a compatible PETSc/MPI installation (typically available in Docker or via conda-forge on supported Unix-like platforms). Native Windows installation is not generally supported. Use linear_solver="iterative" for a SciPy-based alternative without the PETSc dependency.

Temperature is coupled to the Darcy flow: pressure is solved first, a Darcy velocity is computed from its gradient, and that velocity enters the temperature equation as a dw_advect_div_free advection term.

Set include_flow=False to skip the pressure stage entirely and solve pure heat conduction instead -- useful to validate the diffusion term in isolation (e.g. against the known analytical steady-state profile) before trusting the coupled result. Rock units still use porosity-weighted effective conductivity/heat capacity by default in this mode (a static, saturated rock); to also remove the fluid's contribution entirely, set porosity=0.0 on the relevant RockUnitProperties -- the same formulas then reduce exactly to k_solid/rho_c_solid.

mesh_type (which meshing component produced mesh_results -- one of MeshType.IMPLICIT/STRUCTURED/UNSTRUCTURED) is read directly from mesh_results.mesh_type, set automatically by create_implicit_structured_mesh/create_structured_mesh_data/ create_unstructured_mesh_data -- not a separate constructor argument, since that would just be a second place the same fact could go stale or disagree with the actual mesh. Raises clearly if mesh_results.mesh_type is None (e.g. a manually-constructed MeshResults in a test that never set it). All three mesh types work end-to-end for unfaulted models; a structured mesh paired with a faulted structural model is not supported (blocked at the meshing stage, since that combination does not reliably converge -- use implicit or unstructured meshing for faulted models instead).

Limited fault support: pass fault_zone_properties (a RockUnitProperties) to give cells near any fault their own separate material, instead of silently treating them as ordinary lithology. Off by default (None). Faults aren't tagged anywhere on MeshResults for implicit/structured meshes (only a per-block lithology id); only unstructured meshing explicitly meshes fault surfaces, and SfePy itself has no fault/interface element either (only per-region material constants, same as lithology already uses) -- so this represents a fault as a "damage zone" band of cells straddling its trace (fault_zone_n_voxels grid cells wide, computed on the structural model's grid via each fault's get_domain_mask(), then resampled to mesh cells the same way lithology is resampled for unstructured meshes), a standard, simpler proxy for fault hydraulics (gouge seal or fracture-enhanced conduit) than an exact geometric split. All faults in the structural model are combined into one shared "fault zone" material region (Omega_fault) -- not per-fault -- deliberately the smallest useful increment, not a complete fault model. Respects structural_frame.fault_activity though: the structural modeling component supports finite faults that don't cut every stratigraphic group (model9 is the clearest example; a single fault can also be restricted this way via set_fault_activity_by_index/_by_group), and a fault's raw get_domain_mask() doesn't know about that restriction at all (it's a purely geometric scalar_field > scalar_value quantity) -- so the fault-zone trace is masked, per fault, to only the grid cells whose lithology's stratigraphic group that fault is actually active for (group_idx >= fault_activity[name], the same rule effective_domain_components_for_group in general.py uses for the real lith_block computation; basement is always treated as active, since it sits below/outside every group). Setting fault_zone_properties identical to the surrounding rock's properties is a no-op on the result (useful for isolating a suspected fault-zone effect by comparison).
