def restrict_to_kept_cells(mesh: DualContourMesh, cell_kept: npt.NDArray[np.bool_]) -> DualContourMesh:
    """
    The mesh with only the quads all 4 of whose cells are kept.

    The same mesh as :func:`dual_contour` with ``cell_kept`` gives, without a
    second contouring pass: a quad's 4 vertices are its 4 cells' vertices, so
    a quad is kept if all of them are. Only for meshes as :func:`dual_contour`
    returns them (or restricted by this function), whose triangles ``q`` and
    ``q + F // 2`` form quad ``q``.

    Args:
        mesh: A mesh from :func:`dual_contour`.
        cell_kept: Mask of the cells the mesh was contoured on, shape ``(M,)``.

    Returns:
        The kept quads with only the vertices they use, in their original
        order. ``n_missing_quads`` is the unrestricted mesh's.
    """
    kept_vertex = np.asarray(cell_kept, dtype=bool)[mesh.vertex_rows]
    n_quads = mesh.faces.shape[0] // 2
    kept_quad = kept_vertex[mesh.faces[:n_quads]].all(axis=1) & kept_vertex[mesh.faces[n_quads:]].all(axis=1)
    vertices, faces, used = select_faces(mesh.vertices, mesh.faces, np.concatenate([kept_quad, kept_quad]))
    return DualContourMesh(
        vertices=vertices, faces=faces, vertex_cells=mesh.vertex_cells[used], vertex_rows=mesh.vertex_rows[used],
        vertex_at_group_boundary=mesh.vertex_at_group_boundary[used], n_missing_quads=mesh.n_missing_quads,
    )

def select_faces(
        vertices: FloatArray, faces: npt.NDArray[np.integer], keep: npt.NDArray[np.bool_]
) -> Tuple[FloatArray, IntArray, IntArray]:
    """
    The triangles where ``keep`` is True, with only the vertices they use.

    Args:
        vertices: Vertex coordinates, shape ``(V, 3)``.
        faces: Vertex indices of the triangles, shape ``(F, 3)``.
        keep: Which triangles to keep, shape ``(F,)``.

    Returns:
        ``(vertices, faces, used)``: the kept vertices in their original order,
        the kept triangles renumbered to them (int64), and the original index of
        each kept vertex.
    """
    faces = np.asarray(faces, dtype=np.int64).reshape(-1, 3)[np.asarray(keep, dtype=bool)]
    used = np.unique(faces)
    new_index = np.full(np.asarray(vertices).shape[0], -1, dtype=np.int64)
    new_index[used] = np.arange(used.size)
    return np.asarray(vertices)[used], new_index[faces], used

docs.title: Octree refinement
docs.text:
Adaptive refinement and coarsening of an :class:OctreeGrid.

:func:refine_cells: starting from the base blocks (or from given cells), every cell whose 8 corners get different labels is split into its 8 children, level by level, until max_level. Cells whose corners all agree become leaves.

:func:coarsen_cells: the reverse, bottom-up: 8 sibling leaves are merged back into their parent where the labels are identical across the whole parent. This lets a model refine for one purpose (e.g. surfaces needed for meshes) and then store only the cells another purpose needs (e.g. the lithology).

The result of both is a set of cells (:class:OctreeCells) that tiles the extent.

Both can work per fault domain: given the domain of every cell (:data:CellDomains), each point is labelled with the domain of the cell it belongs to, a lattice point shared by cells of different domains is labelled once per domain, and only siblings of one domain are merged (or, with separate merge labels, only siblings with the same merge label).

:func:balance_2to1: refine until face-adjacent cells differ by at most one level.

Ported from the adaptive classification loop of the octree research code (corner-disagreement refinement), adapted to integer cell addresses and a grid of base blocks.

Refine until cells that share a face differ by at most one level (2:1 balance).

Repeatedly splits every leaf that has a face neighbour more than one level finer into its 8 children, until none is left. Only splits, never merges: every cell at max level stays, and the result refines cells.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default grid OctreeGrid

The octree grid.

required cells OctreeCells

Leaf cells that tile the extent.

required

Returns:

Type Description OctreeCells

The balanced leaves. cells itself if it is balanced already.

Source code in core/structural_modeling_components/structural_modeling_utility/octree_refinement.py 
def balance_2to1(grid: OctreeGrid, cells: OctreeCells) -> OctreeCells:
    """
    Refine until cells that share a face differ by at most one level (2:1 balance).

    Repeatedly splits every leaf that has a face neighbour more than one level
    finer into its 8 children, until none is left. Only splits, never merges:
    every cell at max level stays, and the result refines ``cells``.

    Args:
        grid: The octree grid.
        cells: Leaf cells that tile the extent.

    Returns:
        The balanced leaves. ``cells`` itself if it is balanced already.
    """
    level = cells.level.astype(np.int64)
    ijk = cells.ijk.astype(np.int64)
    changed = False
    while True:
        # Level of every finest voxel, and the finest level among its face neighbours.
        level_map = np.empty(grid.finest_resolution, dtype=np.int8)
        for lvl in np.unique(level):
            members = np.flatnonzero(level == lvl)
            n = 2 ** (grid.max_level - int(lvl))
            view = level_map.reshape(level_map.shape[0] // n, n, level_map.shape[1] // n, n,
                                     level_map.shape[2] // n, n)
            view[ijk[members, 0], :, ijk[members, 1], :, ijk[members, 2], :] = lvl
        finer_neighbour = np.full(level_map.shape, -1, dtype=np.int8)
        for axis in range(3):
            lower = [slice(None)] * 3
            upper = [slice(None)] * 3
            lower[axis], upper[axis] = slice(0, -1), slice(1, None)
            np.maximum(finer_neighbour[tuple(lower)], level_map[tuple(upper)], out=finer_neighbour[tuple(lower)])
            np.maximum(finer_neighbour[tuple(upper)], level_map[tuple(lower)], out=finer_neighbour[tuple(upper)])

        split = np.zeros(level.size, dtype=bool)
        for lvl in np.unique(level):
            if lvl >= grid.max_level - 1:
                continue  # no neighbour can be two levels finer
            members = np.flatnonzero(level == lvl)
            n = 2 ** (grid.max_level - int(lvl))
            nx, ny, nz = grid.cells_per_axis(int(lvl))
            finest_near = finer_neighbour.reshape(nx, n, ny, n, nz, n).max(axis=(1, 3, 5))
            split[members] = finest_near[ijk[members, 0], ijk[members, 1], ijk[members, 2]] > lvl + 1
        if not split.any():
            break
        changed = True
        children = (2 * ijk[split])[:, None, :] + CORNER_OFFSETS[None, :, :]
        level = np.concatenate([level[~split], np.repeat(level[split] + 1, 8)])
        ijk = np.concatenate([ijk[~split], children.reshape(-1, 3)])
    if not changed:
        return cells
    return OctreeCells(level=level.astype(np.uint8), ijk=ijk.astype(np.int32))

Split every leaf that shares a face with a max-level leaf down to max level (one pass).

Dual contouring joins max-level cells only, so a surface crossing next to a coarser leaf would leave a gap; so would a surface that grazes a coarse leaf without changing the label at any of its corners. Splitting the coarse neighbours of all max-level leaves closes both kinds of gap in the octree research code's test models. Only one pass: repeated, it floods the whole extent.

Parameters:

required cells OctreeCells

def balance_mesh_depth_adjacency(grid: OctreeGrid, cells: OctreeCells) -> OctreeCells:
    """
    Split every leaf that shares a face with a max-level leaf down to max level (one pass).

    Dual contouring joins max-level cells only, so a surface crossing next to a
    coarser leaf would leave a gap; so would a surface that grazes a coarse leaf
    without changing the label at any of its corners. Splitting the coarse
    neighbours of all max-level leaves closes both kinds of gap in the octree
    research code's test models. Only one pass: repeated, it floods the whole
    extent.

    Args:
        grid: The octree grid.
        cells: Leaf cells that tile the extent.

    Returns:
        The leaves after the split; split leaves are replaced by their max-level
        descendants. Cells keep their positions within a level otherwise.
    """
    from scipy import ndimage

    level = cells.level.astype(np.int64)
    ijk = cells.ijk.astype(np.int64)
    at_max = level == grid.max_level
    if not at_max.any() or at_max.all():
        return cells

    finest = np.zeros(grid.finest_resolution, dtype=bool)
    finest[ijk[at_max, 0], ijk[at_max, 1], ijk[at_max, 2]] = True
    touched = ndimage.binary_dilation(finest, structure=ndimage.generate_binary_structure(3, 1))

    split = np.zeros(level.size, dtype=bool)
    for lvl in np.unique(level[~at_max]):
        members = np.flatnonzero(level == lvl)
        n = 2 ** (grid.max_level - int(lvl))
        nx, ny, nz = grid.cells_per_axis(int(lvl))
        blocks = touched.reshape(nx, n, ny, n, nz, n).any(axis=(1, 3, 5))
        split[members] = blocks[ijk[members, 0], ijk[members, 1], ijk[members, 2]]
    if not split.any():
        return cells

    new_ijk = [ijk[~split]]
    new_level = [level[~split]]
    for lvl in np.unique(level[split]):
        members = np.flatnonzero(split & (level == lvl))
        n = 2 ** (grid.max_level - int(lvl))
        a = np.arange(n)
        offsets = np.stack(np.meshgrid(a, a, a, indexing="ij"), axis=-1).reshape(-1, 3)
        children = (ijk[members] * n)[:, None, :] + offsets[None, :, :]
        new_ijk.append(children.reshape(-1, 3))
        new_level.append(np.full(children.shape[0] * children.shape[1], grid.max_level, dtype=np.int64))
    return OctreeCells(level=np.concatenate(new_level).astype(np.uint8),
                       ijk=np.concatenate(new_ijk).astype(np.int32))

def base_cells(grid: OctreeGrid) -> OctreeCells:
    """All base blocks of ``grid`` as level-0 cells."""
    axes = (np.arange(n) for n in grid.base_resolution)
    ii, jj, kk = np.meshgrid(*axes, indexing="ij")
    ijk = np.column_stack([ii.ravel(), jj.ravel(), kk.ravel()])
    return OctreeCells(level=np.zeros(len(ijk), dtype=np.uint8), ijk=ijk.astype(np.int32))

docs.title: coarsen_cells(grid, cells, label_points, cell_domains=None, merge_labels=None)
docs.text:
Merge sibling leaves back into their parent wherever the labels don't change.

Bottom-up from max_level: when all 8 children of a parent are leaves and every label column is identical at all 27 lattice points of the parent (its corners, edge and face midpoints and center, which are the corners of the 8 children), the children are replaced by the parent. Merged parents can merge again one level up.

Labels never change inside a merged cell at the lattice points checked, so a per-cell quantity derived from the labels (e.g. lithology classified at cell centers) is the same before and after coarsening.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default grid OctreeGrid

The octree grid.

required cells OctreeCells

Leaf cells that tile the extent, e.g. from :func:refine_cells.

required label_points Union[PointLabeler, DomainPointLabeler]

Labels for points; see :data:PointLabeler. With cell_domains a :data:DomainPointLabeler.

required cell_domains Optional[CellDomains]

Domain of each cell; see :data:CellDomains. When given, each child's corners are labelled with the child's domain, and (without merge_labels) only children of one domain are merged.

None merge_labels Optional[CellDomains]

Optional label of each cell, in the form of :data:CellDomains: only children with the same merge label are merged. Lets children of different domains merge where that doesn't matter, while their corners are still labelled with their own domains. Defaults to cell_domains.

None

Returns:

Type Description OctreeCells

The coarsened leaf cells.

Source code in core/structural_modeling_components/structural_modeling_utility/octree_refinement.py 
def coarsen_cells(
        grid: OctreeGrid,
        cells: OctreeCells,
        label_points: Union[PointLabeler, DomainPointLabeler],
        cell_domains: Optional[CellDomains] = None,
        merge_labels: Optional[CellDomains] = None,
) -> OctreeCells:
    """
    Merge sibling leaves back into their parent wherever the labels don't change.

    Bottom-up from ``max_level``: when all 8 children of a parent are leaves and
    every label column is identical at all 27 lattice points of the parent (its
    corners, edge and face midpoints and center, which are the corners of the 8
    children), the children are replaced by the parent. Merged parents can merge
    again one level up.

    Labels never change inside a merged cell at the lattice points checked, so a
    per-cell quantity derived from the labels (e.g. lithology classified at cell
    centers) is the same before and after coarsening.

    Args:
        grid: The octree grid.
        cells: Leaf cells that tile the extent, e.g. from :func:`refine_cells`.
        label_points: Labels for points; see :data:`PointLabeler`. With
            ``cell_domains`` a :data:`DomainPointLabeler`.
        cell_domains: Domain of each cell; see :data:`CellDomains`. When given,
            each child's corners are labelled with the child's domain, and
            (without ``merge_labels``) only children of one domain are merged.
        merge_labels: Optional label of each cell, in the form of
            :data:`CellDomains`: only children with the same merge label are
            merged. Lets children of different domains merge where that doesn't
            matter, while their corners are still labelled with their own
            domains. Defaults to ``cell_domains``.

    Returns:
        The coarsened leaf cells.
    """
    merge_labels = merge_labels if merge_labels is not None else cell_domains
    level = cells.level.astype(np.int64)
    ijk = cells.ijk.astype(np.int64)

    for child_level in range(grid.max_level, 0, -1):
        at_level = np.flatnonzero(level == child_level)
        if at_level.size == 0:
            continue
        parent_level = child_level - 1
        parent_ijk_of_child = ijk[at_level] // 2
        keys = linear_cell_index(parent_ijk_of_child, grid.cells_per_axis(parent_level))
        unique_keys, first, inverse, counts = np.unique(
            keys, return_index=True, return_inverse=True, return_counts=True)
        complete = counts == 8
        if not complete.any():
            continue

        candidates = parent_ijk_of_child[first[complete]]
        one_label = np.ones(candidates.shape[0], dtype=bool)
        if merge_labels is not None:
            child_labels = np.asarray(merge_labels(child_level, ijk[at_level]), dtype=np.int64)
            lowest = np.full(unique_keys.size, np.iinfo(np.int64).max)
            highest = np.full(unique_keys.size, np.iinfo(np.int64).min)
            np.minimum.at(lowest, inverse.ravel(), child_labels)
            np.maximum.at(highest, inverse.ravel(), child_labels)
            one_label = (lowest == highest)[complete]

        # The 8 children of every candidate, and their corners (the parent's 27
        # lattice points), each labelled with its child's domain.
        parent_of = inverse.ravel()
        is_candidate = complete[parent_of]
        order = np.argsort(parent_of[is_candidate], kind="stable")
        children = at_level[is_candidate][order].reshape(-1, 8)
        lattice = (ijk[children][:, :, None, :] + CORNER_OFFSETS[None, None, :, :]).reshape(-1, 64, 3)
        domains = None
        if cell_domains is not None:
            child_domains = np.asarray(cell_domains(child_level, ijk[children.ravel()]), dtype=np.int64)
            domains = np.repeat(child_domains.reshape(-1, 8), 8, axis=1)
        labels = _labels_at_lattice(grid, child_level, lattice, label_points, domains)
        uniform = one_label & np.all(labels == labels[:, :1, :], axis=(1, 2))
        if not uniform.any():
            continue

        merged_parent = np.zeros(unique_keys.size, dtype=bool)
        merged_parent[np.flatnonzero(complete)[uniform]] = True
        drop = at_level[merged_parent[inverse.ravel()]]
        keep = np.ones(level.size, dtype=bool)
        keep[drop] = False
        level = np.concatenate([level[keep], np.full(int(uniform.sum()), parent_level, dtype=np.int64)])
        ijk = np.concatenate([ijk[keep], candidates[uniform]])

    return OctreeCells(level=level.astype(np.uint8), ijk=ijk.astype(np.int32))

def refine_cells(
        grid: OctreeGrid,
        label_points: Union[PointLabeler, DomainPointLabeler],
        start: Optional[OctreeCells] = None,
        cell_domains: Optional[CellDomains] = None,
) -> OctreeCells:
    """
    Refine cells wherever their corner labels disagree.

    Args:
        grid: The octree grid.
        label_points: Labels for points; see :data:`PointLabeler`. Only corner
            points are labelled. With ``cell_domains`` a :data:`DomainPointLabeler`.
        start: Cells to start from, at any levels. Defaults to the base blocks.
            Cells already at ``max_level`` are kept as they are.
        cell_domains: Domain of each cell; see :data:`CellDomains`. When given,
            the corners of a cell are labelled with the cell's domain. Children
            lie inside their parent, so they keep its domain as long as no start
            cell spans two domains.

    Returns:
        The leaf cells. They tile the extent; cells of the same level keep
        the order in which they were created.
    """
    start = start if start is not None else base_cells(grid)
    pending: Dict[int, List[npt.NDArray[np.int64]]] = {}
    for level in np.unique(start.level):
        pending[int(level)] = [start.ijk[start.level == level].astype(np.int64)]

    leaf_levels: List[npt.NDArray[np.uint8]] = []
    leaf_ijk: List[npt.NDArray[np.int64]] = []

    for level in range(grid.max_level + 1):
        if level not in pending:
            continue
        ijk = np.concatenate(pending.pop(level))
        if level == grid.max_level or ijk.shape[0] == 0:
            mixed = np.zeros(ijk.shape[0], dtype=bool)
        else:
            mixed = _corners_disagree(grid, level, ijk, label_points, cell_domains)

        leaf_levels.append(np.full(int((~mixed).sum()), level, dtype=np.uint8))
        leaf_ijk.append(ijk[~mixed])

        if mixed.any():
            children = 2 * ijk[mixed][:, None, :] + CORNER_OFFSETS[None, :, :]
            pending.setdefault(level + 1, []).append(children.reshape(-1, 3))

    return OctreeCells(level=np.concatenate(leaf_levels), ijk=np.concatenate(leaf_ijk).astype(np.int32))

        Isovalues at which to extract surfaces.
    spacing : tuple[float, float, float]
        Voxel spacing in (x, y, z).
    extent : tuple[float, ...]
        Model extent as (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax). The block is
        assumed cell-centred on this extent; vertices are offset by
        ``extent.min + spacing / 2`` to world coordinates.

    Returns
    -------
    mc_vertices : list[np.ndarray]
        Vertex arrays in world coordinates, one per isovalue.
    mc_edges : list[np.ndarray]
        Triangle index arrays, one per isovalue.
    """
    origin = _grid_origin(spacing, extent)
    mc_vertices, mc_edges = [], []
    for level in elements:
        verts, faces, _, _ = measure.marching_cubes(block, float(level), spacing=spacing)
        mc_vertices.append(verts + origin)
        mc_edges.append(faces)
    return mc_vertices, mc_edges

def marching_cubes_per_element(
    block: NDArray[np.float64],
    element: float,
    spacing: Tuple[float, float, float],
    extent: Tuple[float, ...],
    mask: Optional[NDArray[np.bool_]],
) -> Tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.int64]]:
    """
    Extract the surface mesh for a single isovalue from a scalar field.

    Parameters
    ----------
    block : np.ndarray
        3D scalar field array.
    element : float
        Isovalue of the structural element to extract.
    spacing : tuple[float, float, float]
        Voxel spacing in (x, y, z).
    extent : tuple[float, ...]
        Model extent as (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax). The block is
        assumed cell-centred on this extent; vertices are offset by
        ``extent.min + spacing / 2`` to world coordinates.
    mask : np.ndarray or None
        Boolean mask restricting the extraction region. Pass None for no masking.

    Returns
    -------
    vertices : np.ndarray
        Vertex array in world coordinates, shape (N, 3).
        Empty (shape (0, 3)) if the isovalue is not crossed in the masked region.
    edges : np.ndarray
        Triangle index array, shape (M, 3).
        Empty (shape (0, 3)) if the isovalue is not crossed in the masked region.
    """
    # If the scalar field does not cross the iso-value anywhere in the (masked)
    # domain — e.g. a formation absent from one fault block — return empty arrays
    # so the caller can combine or skip them gracefully.
    try:
        verts, edges, _, _ = measure.marching_cubes(block, element, spacing=spacing, mask=mask)
    except RuntimeError:
        return np.empty((0, 3)), np.empty((0, 3), dtype=int)
    vertices = verts + _grid_origin(spacing, extent)
    return vertices, edges

def get_surface_mesh_gradients(
    result: StructuralModelResults,
    norm: bool = True,
    mesh_type: GeoMeshType = GeoMeshType.UNMASKED,
    return_faults: bool = True,
    fault_mesh_type: Optional[FaultMeshType] = None,
) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Dict[str, NDArray[np.float64]]], Dict[str, Dict[str, NDArray[np.float64]]]]:
    """
    Compute gradient vectors at surface mesh vertices by interpolating scalar field gradients.

    Parameters
    ----------
    result : StructuralModelResults
        Computed structural model results.
    norm : bool, default True
        Whether to normalize gradient vectors to unit length.
    mesh_type : GeoMeshType, default GeoMeshType.UNMASKED
        Mesh type to use for structural elements.
    return_faults : bool, default True
        Whether to also compute gradients for fault elements.
    fault_mesh_type : FaultMeshType, optional
        Mesh type to use for fault elements. Defaults to ``mesh_type`` if not set.

    Returns
    -------
    gradients_dict : dict
        ``{element.name: {"points": (N, 3), "vectors": (N, 3)}}``
    gradients_faults_dict : dict
        ``{fault_element.name: {"points": (N, 3), "vectors": (N, 3)}}``
        Empty if no faults or ``return_faults=False``.
    """
    grid = result.structural_frame.grid
    res = grid.resolution

    # grid coords reshaped
    x = grid.grid_coordinates[:, 0].reshape(res)
    y = grid.grid_coordinates[:, 1].reshape(res)
    z = grid.grid_coordinates[:, 2].reshape(res)

    # sort axes for interpolator
    x_sorted_idx = np.argsort(x[:, 0, 0])
    y_sorted_idx = np.argsort(y[0, :, 0])
    z_sorted_idx = np.argsort(z[0, 0, :])

    x_sorted = x[x_sorted_idx, 0, 0]
    y_sorted = y[0, y_sorted_idx, 0]
    z_sorted = z[0, 0, z_sorted_idx]

    def make_interpolators(sf):
        grad = np.gradient(sf)
        gx = grad[0][x_sorted_idx, :, :]
        gy = grad[1][:, y_sorted_idx, :]
        gz = grad[2][:, :, z_sorted_idx]

        ix = RegularGridInterpolator((x_sorted, y_sorted, z_sorted), gx, bounds_error=False, fill_value=None)
        iy = RegularGridInterpolator((x_sorted, y_sorted, z_sorted), gy, bounds_error=False, fill_value=None)
        iz = RegularGridInterpolator((x_sorted, y_sorted, z_sorted), gz, bounds_error=False, fill_value=None)
        return ix, iy, iz

    def interpolate_on_mesh(element, ix, iy, iz, mt):
        pts = element.get_mesh(mt)[0]
        vecs = np.column_stack((ix(pts), iy(pts), iz(pts)))
        if norm:
            vecs = normalize_vectors(vecs)
        return {
            "points": np.asarray(pts),
            "vectors": np.asarray(vecs),
        }

    # --- structural elements ---
    gradients_dict = {}
    for group in result.structural_frame.structural_groups:
        ix, iy, iz = make_interpolators(group.scalar_field)
        for element in group.structural_elements:
            gradients_dict[element.name] = interpolate_on_mesh(element, ix, iy, iz, mesh_type)

    # --- faults (optional) ---
    gradients_faults_dict = {}
    fault_frame = getattr(result.structural_frame, "fault_frame", None)
    _fault_mesh_type = fault_mesh_type if fault_mesh_type is not None else mesh_type

    if return_faults and fault_frame is not None:
        for fault_element in fault_frame.fault_elements:
            ix, iy, iz = make_interpolators(fault_element.scalar_field)
            gradients_faults_dict[fault_element.name] = interpolate_on_mesh(
                fault_element, ix, iy, iz, _fault_mesh_type
            )

    return gradients_dict, gradients_faults_dict

def normalize_vectors(vectors: NDArray[np.float64]) -> NDArray[np.float64]:
    """
    Normalize an array of vectors to unit length.

    Parameters
    ----------
    vectors : np.ndarray
        Array of shape (N, 3).

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        Row-normalized array of shape (N, 3). Zero-norm rows are left unchanged.
    """
    norms = np.linalg.norm(vectors, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    return vectors / np.where(norms == 0, 1, norms)

def plot_surface_mesh_gradients(
    structural_model_result: StructuralModelResults,
    gradients_dict: Dict[str, Dict[str, NDArray[np.float64]]],
    gradients_faults_dict: Optional[Dict[str, Dict[str, NDArray[np.float64]]]] = None,
    mesh_type: GeoMeshType = GeoMeshType.UNMASKED,
    scale_factor: float = 50,
) -> None:
    """
    Plot gradient vector fields at surface mesh vertices using PyVista.

    Parameters
    ----------
    structural_model_result : StructuralModelResults
        The computed structural model results (used for mesh and color lookup).
    gradients_dict : dict
        Gradient data for structural elements, as returned by
        :func:`get_surface_mesh_gradients`.
    gradients_faults_dict : dict, optional
        Gradient data for fault elements. If None, faults are not plotted.
    mesh_type : GeoMeshType, default GeoMeshType.UNMASKED
        Mesh type used to retrieve element meshes for wireframe overlay.
    scale_factor : float, default 50
        Arrow scale factor for gradient glyphs.
    """
    plotter = pv.Plotter()

    for i, element in enumerate(gradients_dict.keys()):
        pdata = pv.PolyData(gradients_dict[element]['points'])
        pdata["vectors"] = gradients_dict[element]['vectors']

        arrows = pdata.glyph(orient="vectors", scale="vectors", factor=scale_factor)
        plotter.add_mesh(arrows, color=structural_model_result.structural_frame.get_element_by_name(element).color)

        plotter.add_mesh(
            pv.PolyData(structural_model_result.structural_frame.get_element_by_name(element).get_mesh(mesh_type)[0],
                        np.insert(structural_model_result.structural_frame.get_element_by_name(element)
                                  .get_mesh(mesh_type)[1], 0, 3, axis=1).ravel()),
            color=structural_model_result.structural_frame.get_element_by_name(element).color, style="wireframe")

    if gradients_faults_dict is not None:
        for i, fault_element in enumerate(gradients_faults_dict.keys()):
            pdata = pv.PolyData(gradients_faults_dict[fault_element]['points'])
            pdata["vectors"] = gradients_faults_dict[fault_element]['vectors']

            arrows = pdata.glyph(orient="vectors", scale="vectors", factor=scale_factor)
            plotter.add_mesh(arrows,
                             color=structural_model_result.structural_frame.fault_frame.get_element_by_name(
                                 fault_element).color)

            plotter.add_mesh(
                pv.PolyData(
                    structural_model_result.structural_frame.fault_frame.get_element_by_name(fault_element).get_mesh(
                        mesh_type)[0],
                    np.insert(structural_model_result.structural_frame.fault_frame.get_element_by_name(fault_element)
                              .get_mesh(mesh_type)[1], 0, 3, axis=1).ravel()),
                color=structural_model_result.structural_frame.fault_frame.get_element_by_name(fault_element).color,
                style="wireframe")

    plotter.show()

def plot_fault_input_data_3D(
        input_data: InputData_FaultElements,
        *,
        show_orientations: bool = True,
        arrow_scale: Optional[float] = None,
        point_size: int = 8,
        notebook: bool = False,
        show: bool = True,
) -> pv.Plotter:
    """
    3D PyVista plot of raw fault input data (surface points + orientations),
    colored by fault name.  No FaultFrame required.
    """
    pv.global_theme.allow_empty_mesh = True
    plotter = pv.Plotter(notebook=notebook)

    sp = input_data.fault_surface_points
    ori = input_data.fault_orientations
    fault_names = input_data.fault_names

    fault_cmap = plt.get_cmap("tab10")
    color_map = {
        name: to_hex(fault_cmap(i / max(len(fault_names), 1))[:3])
        for i, name in enumerate(fault_names)
    }

    if arrow_scale is None and show_orientations and ori is not None and not ori.empty:
        arrow_scale = _orientation_arrow_length(None, np.vstack([sp[["X", "Y", "Z"]].values, ori[["X", "Y", "Z"]].values]))

    legend_entries: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for fault_name in fault_names:
        color = color_map.get(fault_name, "grey")
        legend_entries.append((fault_name, color))

        df_pts = sp[sp["formation"] == fault_name]
        if not df_pts.empty:
            cloud = pv.PolyData(df_pts[["X", "Y", "Z"]].values.astype(np.float64))
            plotter.add_points(cloud, color=color, point_size=point_size, render_points_as_spheres=True)

        if show_orientations and ori is not None and not ori.empty:
            df_ori = ori[ori["formation"] == fault_name]
            for _, row in df_ori.iterrows():
                plotter.add_mesh(
                    pv.Arrow(
                        start=row[["X", "Y", "Z"]].values.astype(float),
                        direction=row[["G_x", "G_y", "G_z"]].values.astype(float),
                        scale=arrow_scale,
                    ),
                    color=color,
                )

    pts = sp[["X", "Y", "Z"]].values
    ranges = pts.max(axis=0) - pts.min(axis=0)
    margin = ranges * 0.05
    bounds = (
        pts[:, 0].min() - margin[0], pts[:, 0].max() + margin[0],
        pts[:, 1].min() - margin[1], pts[:, 1].max() + margin[1],
        pts[:, 2].min() - margin[2], pts[:, 2].max() + margin[2],
    )
    plotter.show_bounds(bounds=bounds, location="furthest", grid=True)

    plotter.add_legend(labels=legend_entries, size=(0.20, 0.18), loc="lower right", face="rectangle")
    plotter.camera.view_angle = 30.0
    plotter.camera.azimuth = 25.0
    plotter.camera.elevation = -15.0

    if show:
        plotter.show()
    return plotter

docs.title: plot_fault_model_2D(fault_frame, *, axis='y', index=None, show_results=True, show_input_data=True, show_fault_contours=True, show_grid=False)
docs.text:
2D slice plot for a FaultFrame.

  • Domain-map coloring (show_results) and fault contours (show_fault_contours) are independent: domain blocks need a computed domain_map (absent for a cross-cutting fault model -- see compute_fault_domains -- in which case a UserWarning is raised and domain blocks are skipped), but fault contours only need each fault's own scalar_field/scalar_value, which are always set regardless of cross-cutting, so they're drawn whenever requested.
  • Input data (points/orientations) is shown independently of both, if present.
  • With show_grid=True: outlines the grid cells the slice cuts (the fault cells on an octree), with or without a domain map.

Extent is computed from the cell-center coordinates with half-cell padding, so imshow/contour align properly. On an octree, index and the centers refer to the finest resolution.

Source code in core/structural_modeling_components/structural_modeling_visualization/structural_modeling_visualization.py 
def plot_fault_model_2D(
        fault_frame: FaultFrame,
        *,
        axis: Literal['x', 'y', 'z'] = "y",
        index: Optional[int] = None,
        show_results: bool = True,
        show_input_data: bool = True,
        show_fault_contours: bool = True,
        show_grid: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """
    2D slice plot for a FaultFrame.

    - Domain-map coloring (show_results) and fault contours (show_fault_contours)
      are independent: domain blocks need a computed domain_map (absent for a
      cross-cutting fault model -- see compute_fault_domains -- in which case a
      UserWarning is raised and domain blocks are skipped), but fault contours
      only need each fault's own scalar_field/scalar_value, which are always set
      regardless of cross-cutting, so they're drawn whenever requested.
    - Input data (points/orientations) is shown independently of both, if present.
    - With show_grid=True: outlines the grid cells the slice cuts (the fault
      cells on an octree), with or without a domain map.

    Extent is computed from the cell-center coordinates with half-cell padding,
    so imshow/contour align properly. On an octree, ``index`` and the centers
    refer to the finest resolution.
    """

    assert axis in ("x", "y", "z"), "Axis must be 'x', 'y', or 'z'."

    if fault_frame.grid is None:
        raise ValueError("FaultFrame has no grid associated.")

    grid = fault_frame.grid

    x, y, z = _axis_centers(grid)

    n_cells = {'x': len(x), 'y': len(y), 'z': len(z)}[axis]
    if index is None:
        index = n_cells // 2
    elif not 0 <= index < n_cells:
        raise ValueError(f"index={index} is outside the grid: along {axis} it must be between 0 and {n_cells - 1}.")

    # spacing for half-cell padded extent
    dx = (x[-1] - x[0]) / (len(x) - 1) if len(x) > 1 else 1.0
    dy = (y[-1] - y[0]) / (len(y) - 1) if len(y) > 1 else 1.0
    dz = (z[-1] - z[0]) / (len(z) - 1) if len(z) > 1 else 1.0

    # mapping to np.take axis (same as your inspiration)
    dim = {"x": 0, "y": 1, "z": 2}[axis]

    if axis == "x":
        extent = (y[0] - dy / 2, y[-1] + dy / 2, z[0] - dz / 2, z[-1] + dz / 2)
        Xc, Yc = np.meshgrid(y, z, indexing="ij")  # for contour coordinates
        xlabel, ylabel = "Y", "Z"
    elif axis == "y":
        extent = (x[0] - dx / 2, x[-1] + dx / 2, z[0] - dz / 2, z[-1] + dz / 2)
        Xc, Yc = np.meshgrid(x, z, indexing="ij")
        xlabel, ylabel = "X", "Z"
    else:  # "z"
        extent = (x[0] - dx / 2, x[-1] + dx / 2, y[0] - dy / 2, y[-1] + dy / 2)
        Xc, Yc = np.meshgrid(x, y, indexing="ij")
        xlabel, ylabel = "X", "Y"

    domain_map = fault_frame.domain_map
    faults = fault_frame.fault_elements or []

    has_result = show_results and domain_map is not None and np.size(domain_map) > 0
    if show_results and not has_result:
        warnings.warn(
            "show_results=True but no domain_map found: the fault model has not "
            "been computed yet (compute_fault_domains), or it is cross-cutting, "
            "where domaining is skipped -- domain blocks won't be plotted. Fault "
            "contours still will be, if show_fault_contours.",
            UserWarning,
        )

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

    # ---------------------------
    # RESULTS: domain map
    # ---------------------------
    if has_result:
        domain_slice = fault_frame.section(domain_map, dim, index).T

        domain_values = np.unique(domain_slice)
        domain_values = domain_values[~np.isnan(domain_values)]

        if len(domain_values) > 0:
            base_cmap = plt.get_cmap("Set3")
            colors = base_cmap(np.linspace(0, 1, len(domain_values)))
            cmap = ListedColormap(colors)
            bounds = np.append(domain_values, domain_values[-1] + 1)
            norm = BoundaryNorm(bounds, cmap.N)

            im = ax.imshow(
                domain_slice,
                origin="lower",
                extent=extent,
                cmap=cmap,
                norm=norm,
                alpha=1.0,
            )
            cbar = plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, ticks=domain_values)
            cbar.set_label("Fault Domain")

    if show_grid:
        _draw_section_cells(ax, fault_frame, dim, index)

    # ---------------------------
    # Fault contours -- independent of domain_map: each fault's own
    # scalar_field/scalar_value is set regardless of cross-cutting (see
    # compute_fault_domains), so these can always be drawn when requested,
    # the same way plot_fault_model_3D's surface meshes don't depend on
    # domain_map either.
    # ---------------------------
    if show_fault_contours:
        handles = []
        for fault in faults:
            sf = fault.scalar_field
            sv = fault.scalar_value
            if sf is None or sv is None:
                continue

            f_slice = fault_frame.section(sf, dim, index).T
            fcol = fault.color or "black"

            CS = ax.contour(
                Xc, Yc,
                f_slice.T,
                levels=[sv],
                colors=[fcol],
                linewidths=1.5,
                linestyles="-",
            )

            # label directly on contour line
            ax.clabel(
                CS,
                fmt={sv: getattr(fault, "name", "fault")},
                inline=True,
                fontsize=15
            )

            handles.append(plt.Line2D([0], [0], color=fcol, lw=1.5, label=getattr(fault, "name", "fault")))

        if handles:
            by_label = {h.get_label(): h for h in handles}
            ax.legend(by_label.values(), by_label.keys(), title="Faults", loc="lower left")

    # ---------------------------
    # INPUT DATA ONLY (project all points)
    # ---------------------------

    if show_input_data:
        for fault in faults:
            # Preferred: dataframe getter (X,Y,Z)
            getter = fault_frame.get_surface_points_for_element
            if getter is not None:
                df_pts = getter(getattr(fault, "name", "fault"))

                if df_pts is None or getattr(df_pts, "empty", False):
                    continue

                fcol = fault.color or "black"
                if axis == "x":
                    ax.scatter(df_pts["Y"], df_pts["Z"], color=fcol, s=30,
                               edgecolors="black", linewidths=0.5, label=getattr(fault, "name", "fault"))
                elif axis == "y":
                    ax.scatter(df_pts["X"], df_pts["Z"], color=fcol, s=30,
                               edgecolors="black", linewidths=0.5, label=getattr(fault, "name", "fault"))
                else:  # z
                    ax.scatter(df_pts["X"], df_pts["Y"], color=fcol, s=30,
                               edgecolors="black", linewidths=0.5, label=getattr(fault, "name", "fault"))

            # ---- orientations as arrows (optional, if getter exists and data present) ----
            ori_getter = fault_frame.get_orientations_for_element
            if ori_getter is not None:
                df_ori = ori_getter(getattr(fault, "name", "fault"))
                if df_ori is not None and not getattr(df_ori, "empty", False):
                    df_ori = _with_unit_gradients(df_ori)
                    if axis == "x":
                        xs, ys, u, v = df_ori["Y"], df_ori["Z"], df_ori["G_y"], df_ori["G_z"]
                    elif axis == "y":
                        xs, ys, u, v = df_ori["X"], df_ori["Z"], df_ori["G_x"], df_ori["G_z"]
                    else:  # z
                        xs, ys, u, v = df_ori["X"], df_ori["Y"], df_ori["G_x"], df_ori["G_y"]

                    ax.quiver(
                        xs, ys, u, v,
                        angles="xy", scale_units="xy", scale=1 / _orientation_arrow_length(grid, None),
                        width=0.01, headwidth=3, headlength=4, headaxislength=3,
                        color=fcol, edgecolors="black", linewidths=0.5,
                        zorder=11,  # above imshow + points
                    )

        # optional: tidy legend (avoid duplicates)
        handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
        by_label = {lab: h for h, lab in zip(handles, labels)}
        if by_label:
            ax.legend(by_label.values(), by_label.keys(), title="Input data", loc="lower left")

    # --- cosmetics ---
    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel)
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
    ax.set_title(f"{axis.upper()} Slice @ index {index}")
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.set_xlim(extent[0], extent[1])
    ax.set_ylim(extent[2], extent[3])

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

def plot_fault_model_3D(
    fault_frame: FaultFrame,
    mesh_type: FaultMeshType = FaultMeshType.UNMASKED,
    show_surface_meshes: bool = True,
    show_input_data: bool = True,
    show_domain_map: bool = True,
    domain_opacity: float = 0.15,
    highlight_crosscuts: bool = True,
    crosscut_color: str = "red",
    crosscut_line_width: float = 6.0,
    notebook: bool = False,
    show: bool = True,
) -> pv.Plotter:
    """
    3D PyVista plot of a fault model with domain map, fault meshes, input data,
    and (where two fault surfaces actually cross) a highlighted crosscut line.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fault_frame : FaultFrame
        Fault frame to visualize.
    mesh_type : FaultMeshType, default FaultMeshType.UNMASKED
        Mesh type for fault surfaces.
    show_surface_meshes : bool, default True
        Whether to render fault surface meshes.
    show_input_data : bool, default True
        Whether to render input surface points and orientation arrows.
    show_domain_map : bool, default True
        Whether to render translucent domain blocks.
    domain_opacity : float, default 0.15
        Opacity of domain block visualizations.
    highlight_crosscuts : bool, default True
        If True (and show_surface_meshes), computes the exact 3D curve(s)
        where any two fault surfaces actually intersect (via PyVista/VTK's
        surface-surface intersection, not a voxel approximation) and draws
        them in crosscut_color. This is purely geometric -- it doesn't need
        to be told whether the model cross-cuts (e.g. via FaultModelResults.
        cross_cutting): a pair of faults that don't cross yields an empty
        intersection and nothing extra is drawn, so this is a no-op for an
        ordinary, non-cross-cutting model and only has an effect when two
        fault surfaces genuinely cross.
    crosscut_color : str, default "red"
        Color for the highlighted crosscut line(s).
    crosscut_line_width : float, default 6.0
        Line width for the highlighted crosscut line(s).
    notebook : bool, default False
        Use off-screen/notebook mode for PyVista.
    show : bool, default True
        Call plotter.show() at the end. Set False to add further actors before displaying.

    Returns
    -------
    pv.Plotter
        The PyVista plotter instance (useful when show=False).
    """
    pv.global_theme.allow_empty_mesh = True
    plotter = pv.Plotter(notebook=notebook)

    legend_entries_faults = []
    legend_entries_domains = []
    legend_entries_crosscuts = []
    fault_meshes: dict[str, pv.PolyData] = {}

    faults = fault_frame.fault_elements or []

    # -------------------------
    # (A) Domain map as translucent voxel blocks (optional)
    # -------------------------
    domain_map = fault_frame.domain_map
    grid = fault_frame.grid

    if show_domain_map and domain_map is not None and grid is not None and isinstance(grid, OctreeGrid):
        # One hexahedron per fault cell, with its domain id as cell data.
        dm = np.asarray(domain_map)
        img = _octree_hexahedra(grid, fault_frame.cells)
        img.cell_data["domain"] = dm.ravel().astype(np.float32)
    elif show_domain_map and domain_map is not None and grid is not None:
        # Get coordinate vectors (same pattern as your 2D)
        def _get_coord(obj, name):
            val = getattr(obj, name, None)
            if val is not None:
                return val
            sub = obj.grid
            if sub is not None:
                return getattr(sub, name, None)
            return None

        x = np.asarray(_get_coord(grid, "gridx"))
        y = np.asarray(_get_coord(grid, "gridy"))
        z = np.asarray(_get_coord(grid, "gridz"))

        # spacing + origin aligned to your 2D half-cell padding convention
        dx = (x[-1] - x[0]) / (len(x) - 1) if len(x) > 1 else 1.0
        dy = (y[-1] - y[0]) / (len(y) - 1) if len(y) > 1 else 1.0
        dz = (z[-1] - z[0]) / (len(z) - 1) if len(z) > 1 else 1.0

        origin = (x[0] - dx / 2, y[0] - dy / 2, z[0] - dz / 2)
        spacing = (dx, dy, dz)

        dm = np.asarray(domain_map)
        # dm is assumed shaped (nx, ny, nz) as cell values
        nx, ny, nz = dm.shape

        # VTK ImageData uses POINT dimensions; cell dims are (nx,ny,nz) => point dims (nx+1,ny+1,nz+1)
        img = pv.ImageData(
            dimensions=(nx + 1, ny + 1, nz + 1),
            spacing=spacing,
            origin=origin,
        )

        # Attach as CELL data. Ordering can be tricky; this is the most common working default.
        # If colors look permuted/swapped, change order='F' to order='C'.
        img.cell_data["domain"] = dm.ravel(order="F").astype(np.float32)

    if show_domain_map and domain_map is not None and grid is not None:
        # Discrete domain colors like the 2D logic (Set3)
        domain_values = np.unique(dm)
        domain_values = domain_values[~np.isnan(domain_values)]
        domain_values = np.array(sorted(domain_values))

        if len(domain_values) > 0:
            base_cmap = plt.get_cmap("Set3")
            colors = base_cmap(np.linspace(0, 1, len(domain_values)))

            # Render each domain as a translucent block
            for i, dv in enumerate(domain_values):
                color = tuple(colors[i, :3])  # RGB

                # threshold around the discrete id
                th = img.threshold(
                    (float(dv) - 0.5, float(dv) + 0.5),
                    scalars="domain"
                )

                if th.n_cells == 0:
                    continue

                # show as filled voxels (no edges) with low opacity tint
                plotter.add_mesh(
                    th,
                    color=color,
                    opacity=domain_opacity,
                    show_edges=False,
                    lighting=False,
                )

                legend_entries_domains.append((f"■ Domain {int(dv) if float(dv).is_integer() else dv}", color))

    # -------------------------
    # (B) Fault meshes + input data
    # -------------------------
    for fault in faults:
        fcol = fault.color or "black"
        fname = getattr(fault, "name", "fault")

        # mesh (optional, skip cleanly if not computed)
        if show_surface_meshes:
            verts = fault.vertices
            edges = fault.edges
            fv = verts.get(mesh_type) if isinstance(verts, dict) else None
            ff = edges.get(mesh_type) if isinstance(edges, dict) else None

            if fv is not None and ff is not None and len(fv) > 0 and len(ff) > 0:
                faces_flat = _faces_to_vtk(np.asarray(ff))
                try:
                    mesh = pv.PolyData(np.asarray(fv), faces_flat)
                except Exception:
                    mesh = pv.PolyData(np.asarray(fv), faces_flat.astype(np.int64, copy=False))

                plotter.add_mesh(mesh, color=fcol, name=fname, label=fname)
                legend_entries_faults.append((f"• {fname}", fcol))
                fault_meshes[fname] = mesh

        # points (optional, show even if no meshes)
        if show_input_data and fault_frame.fault_surface_points_df is not None:
            df_points = fault_frame.get_surface_points_for_element(fname)
            if df_points is not None and not df_points.empty:
                cloud = pv.PolyData(df_points[["X", "Y", "Z"]].values.astype(np.float64))
                plotter.add_points(
                    cloud,
                    color=fcol,
                    point_size=8,
                    render_points_as_spheres=True
                )

        # orientations (optional, show even if no meshes)
        if show_input_data and fault_frame.fault_orientations_df is not None:
            df_ori = fault_frame.get_orientations_for_element(fname)
            if df_ori is not None and not df_ori.empty:
                start = df_ori[["X", "Y", "Z"]].values
                direction = df_ori[["G_x", "G_y", "G_z"]].values

                scale = _orientation_arrow_length(grid, start)
                for i in range(len(start)):
                    arrow = pv.Arrow(start=start[i], direction=direction[i], scale=scale)
                    plotter.add_mesh(arrow, color=fcol)

    # Computed, but no fault has the requested mesh (before computing there are none at all).
    available = sorted({str(t) for f in faults for t in (f.vertices or {})})
    if show_surface_meshes and available and not fault_meshes:
        warnings.warn(f"mesh_type={mesh_type.value!r}: no fault has this mesh; available: {', '.join(available)} "
                      f"(fault MASKED and EXTENDED_MASKED exist only after compute_structural_model). "
                      f"Plotting without fault surfaces.", stacklevel=2)

    # -------------------------
    # (B2) Crosscut lines -- exact surface-surface intersection (optional)
    # -------------------------
    # Purely geometric: a non-crossing pair of fault surfaces has an empty
    # intersection, so this only ever draws something for a genuinely
    # cross-cutting pair -- no need to consult FaultModelResults.cross_cutting
    # or domain_map here, which plot_fault_model_3D never receives anyway
    # (it's only given the FaultFrame).
    if highlight_crosscuts and show_surface_meshes and len(fault_meshes) >= 2:
        # vtkIntersectionPolyDataFilter logs a "No Intersection between
        # objects" warning to the console for every non-crossing pair --
        # expected and harmless (most pairs in an ordinary model don't
        # cross), but noisy. Scoped off only for this loop, restored after.
        from vtkmodules.vtkCommonCore import vtkObject
        _prev_vtk_warnings = vtkObject.GetGlobalWarningDisplay()
        vtkObject.GlobalWarningDisplayOff()
        try:
            for (name_i, mesh_i), (name_j, mesh_j) in itertools.combinations(fault_meshes.items(), 2):
                try:
                    line, _, _ = mesh_i.intersection(mesh_j, split_first=False, split_second=False)
                except Exception:
                    continue  # degenerate/non-manifold mesh pair -- skip rather than fail the whole plot

                if line.n_points == 0 or line.n_cells == 0:
                    continue  # these two faults don't actually cross

                plotter.add_mesh(
                    line,
                    color=crosscut_color,
                    line_width=crosscut_line_width,
                    render_lines_as_tubes=True,
                    name=f"crosscut_{name_i}_{name_j}",
                    label=f"{name_i} x {name_j} crosscut",
                )
                legend_entries_crosscuts.append((f"— {name_i} × {name_j}", crosscut_color))
        finally:
            vtkObject.SetGlobalWarningDisplay(_prev_vtk_warnings)

    # -------------------------
    # (C) Legend (Domains + Faults + Crosscuts)
    # -------------------------
    flat_legend = []
    if legend_entries_domains:
        flat_legend.append(("Domains", "black"))
        flat_legend.extend(legend_entries_domains)

    if legend_entries_faults:
        flat_legend.append(("Faults", "black"))
        flat_legend.extend(legend_entries_faults)

    if legend_entries_crosscuts:
        flat_legend.append(("Crosscuts", "black"))
        flat_legend.extend(legend_entries_crosscuts)

    if flat_legend:
        plotter.add_legend(
            labels=flat_legend,
            size=(0.28, 0.28),
            loc="lower right",
            face="rectangle",
        )

    # -------------------------
    # (D) Bounds + camera
    # -------------------------
    if grid is not None:
        plotter.show_bounds(bounds=grid.extent, location="furthest", grid=True)

    plotter.camera.view_angle = 30.0
    plotter.camera.azimuth = 25.0
    plotter.camera.elevation = -15.0

    if show:
        plotter.show()
    return plotter

def plot_input_data_3D(
        input_data: InputData_StructuralElements,
        *,
        show_orientations: bool = True,
        arrow_scale: Optional[float] = None,
        point_size: int = 8,
        notebook: bool = False,
        show: bool = True,
) -> pv.Plotter:
    """
    3D PyVista plot of raw structural input data (surface points + orientations),
    colored by formation.  No StructuralFrame required.
    """
    pv.global_theme.allow_empty_mesh = True
    plotter = pv.Plotter(notebook=notebook)

    sp = input_data.surface_points
    ori = input_data.orientations
    mapping = input_data.mapping_object  # {group_name: (elem1, elem2, ...)}

    color_map = _make_formation_color_map(mapping)

    if arrow_scale is None and show_orientations and ori is not None and not ori.empty:
        arrow_scale = _orientation_arrow_length(None, np.vstack([sp[["X", "Y", "Z"]].values, ori[["X", "Y", "Z"]].values]))

    legend_entries: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for group_name, elements in mapping.items():
        legend_entries.append((group_name, "black"))
        for el_name in elements:
            color = color_map.get(el_name, "grey")
            legend_entries.append((f"• {el_name}", color))

            df_pts = sp[sp["formation"] == el_name]
            if not df_pts.empty:
                cloud = pv.PolyData(df_pts[["X", "Y", "Z"]].values.astype(np.float64))
                plotter.add_points(cloud, color=color, point_size=point_size, render_points_as_spheres=True)

            if show_orientations and ori is not None and not ori.empty:
                df_ori = ori[ori["formation"] == el_name]
                for _, row in df_ori.iterrows():
                    plotter.add_mesh(
                        pv.Arrow(
                            start=row[["X", "Y", "Z"]].values.astype(float),
                            direction=row[["G_x", "G_y", "G_z"]].values.astype(float),
                            scale=arrow_scale,
                        ),
                        color=color,
                    )

    pts = sp[["X", "Y", "Z"]].values
    ranges = pts.max(axis=0) - pts.min(axis=0)
    margin = ranges * 0.05
    bounds = (
        pts[:, 0].min() - margin[0], pts[:, 0].max() + margin[0],
        pts[:, 1].min() - margin[1], pts[:, 1].max() + margin[1],
        pts[:, 2].min() - margin[2], pts[:, 2].max() + margin[2],
    )
    plotter.show_bounds(bounds=bounds, location="furthest", grid=True)

    plotter.add_legend(labels=legend_entries, size=(0.22, 0.25), loc="lower right", face="rectangle")
    plotter.camera.view_angle = 30.0
    plotter.camera.azimuth = 25.0
    plotter.camera.elevation = -15.0

    if show:
        plotter.show()
    return plotter

def plot_structural_model_2D(
        frame: StructuralFrame,
        *,
        axis: Literal['x', 'y', 'z'] = 'y',
        index: Optional[int] = None,
        show_result: bool = True,
        show_fault_contours: bool = True,
        show_input_data: bool = True,
        show_grid: bool = False,
        title_suffix: str = "",
) -> None:
    """
    2D slice plot of a structural model showing lithology block, scalar contours, and input data.

    Parameters
    ----------
    frame : StructuralFrame
        Structural frame to visualize.
    axis : {'x', 'y', 'z'}, default 'y'
        Axis along which to slice.
    index : int, optional
        Slice index along the chosen axis, at the finest resolution on an
        octree. Defaults to the mid-point.
    show_result : bool, default True
        Overlay the lithology block as a colored background if available.
    show_fault_contours : bool, default True
        Overlay fault isolines from their scalar fields.
    show_input_data : bool, default True
        Overlay input surface points and orientation arrows.
    show_grid : bool, default False
        Outline the grid cells the slice cuts: uniform voxels on a regular
        grid, cells of different sizes on an octree.
    title_suffix : str, default ""
        Optional string appended to the plot title.
    """
    warnings.simplefilter("always", UserWarning)

    assert axis in ('x', 'y', 'z'), "Axis must be 'x', 'y', or 'z'."

    dim = {'x': 0, 'y': 1, 'z': 2}[axis]

    x, y, z = _axis_centers(frame.grid)

    n_cells = {'x': len(x), 'y': len(y), 'z': len(z)}[axis]
    if index is None:
        index = n_cells // 2
    elif not 0 <= index < n_cells:
        raise ValueError(f"index={index} is outside the grid: along {axis} it must be between 0 and {n_cells - 1}.")

    #  Compute spacing for imshow extent
    dx = (x[-1] - x[0]) / (len(x) - 1)
    dy = (y[-1] - y[0]) / (len(y) - 1)
    dz = (z[-1] - z[0]) / (len(z) - 1)

    if axis == 'x':
        extent = (
            y[0] - dy / 2, y[-1] + dy / 2,
            z[0] - dz / 2, z[-1] + dz / 2
        )
        x_coords, y_coords = np.meshgrid(y, z, indexing='ij')
    elif axis == 'y':
        extent = (
            x[0] - dx / 2, x[-1] + dx / 2,
            z[0] - dz / 2, z[-1] + dz / 2
        )
        x_coords, y_coords = np.meshgrid(x, z, indexing='ij')
    else:  # 'z'
        extent = (
            x[0] - dx / 2, x[-1] + dx / 2,
            y[0] - dy / 2, y[-1] + dy / 2
        )
        x_coords, y_coords = np.meshgrid(x, y, indexing='ij')

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

    # ---- lithology (optional) ----
    if show_result:
        has_result = (
            frame.lith_block is not None
            and np.size(frame.lith_block) > 0
        )
        if has_result is False:
            warnings.warn(
                "show_result=True but no lithology block found: the structural model "
                "has not been computed yet (compute_structural_model). Plotting input data only.",
                UserWarning
            )
        else:
            id_to_color, id_to_label = _lithology_colors(frame)
            if frame.lith_block is not None:
                slice_lith = frame.section(frame.lith_block, dim, index)
                slice_lith = slice_lith.T

                sorted_ids = sorted(id_to_color)
                colors = [id_to_color[i] for i in sorted_ids]
                cmap = ListedColormap(colors)
                norm = BoundaryNorm(sorted_ids + [sorted_ids[-1] + 1], len(colors))
                ax.imshow(slice_lith, origin='lower', cmap=cmap, norm=norm, extent=extent, alpha=1, zorder=-100)

    if show_grid:
        _draw_section_cells(ax, frame, dim, index)

    # ---- faults as contours from their scalar fields ----
    if show_fault_contours and frame.fault_frame is not None:
        for fault_index, fault in enumerate(frame.fault_frame.fault_elements):
            f_sf = fault.scalar_field
            f_sv = fault.scalar_value
            if f_sf is None or f_sv is None:
                continue
            f_slice = frame.fault_frame.section(f_sf, dim, index).T

            # if a result was already computed
            if show_result and frame.lith_block is not None:
                # this mask is the age mask defined by youngest group affected by this fault
                group_index = frame.fault_activity_verbose[fault.name]["youngest_group_index"] - 1
                if group_index >= 0:
                    fault_mask = frame.section(frame.structural_groups[group_index].get_mask(), dim, index).T
                else:
                    fault_mask = np.zeros_like(f_slice, dtype=bool)

                f_slice_masked = np.ma.array(f_slice, mask=fault_mask)
            else:
                # Fallback to unmasked contour if no result or mask available
                f_slice_masked = f_slice
            fcol = fault.color or "black"
            CSf = ax.contour(x_coords, y_coords, f_slice_masked.T, levels=[f_sv], colors=[fcol], linewidths=1.5,
                             linestyles="-", zorder=10000)
            ax.clabel(CSf, fmt={f_sv: f"{fault.name}"}, fontsize=15)

    # ---- input data (optional) ----
    if show_input_data:
        for group in frame.structural_groups:
            for elem in group.structural_elements:
                df_pts = frame.get_surface_points_for_element(elem.name)
                df_ori = frame.get_orientations_for_element(elem.name)

                if df_pts is not None and not df_pts.empty:
                    if axis == 'x':
                        ax.scatter(df_pts["Y"], df_pts["Z"], color=elem.color, s=30, edgecolors='black', linewidths=0.5)
                    elif axis == 'y':
                        ax.scatter(df_pts["X"], df_pts["Z"], color=elem.color, s=30, edgecolors='black', linewidths=0.5)
                    else:
                        ax.scatter(df_pts["X"], df_pts["Y"], color=elem.color, s=30, edgecolors='black', linewidths=0.5)

                if df_ori is not None and not df_ori.empty:
                    df_ori = _with_unit_gradients(df_ori)
                    if axis == 'x':
                        xs, ys, u, v = df_ori["Y"], df_ori["Z"], df_ori["G_y"], df_ori["G_z"]
                    elif axis == 'y':
                        xs, ys, u, v = df_ori["X"], df_ori["Z"], df_ori["G_x"], df_ori["G_z"]
                    else:
                        xs, ys, u, v = df_ori["X"], df_ori["Y"], df_ori["G_x"], df_ori["G_y"]

                    ax.quiver(xs, ys, u, v,
                              angles='xy', scale_units='xy', scale=1 / _orientation_arrow_length(frame.grid, None),
                              width=0.01, headwidth=3, headlength=4, headaxislength=3,
                              color=elem.color, edgecolors='black', linewidths=0.5)

    # ---- legend (group bold + elements) ----
    axis_labels = {'x': ("Y", "Z"), 'y': ("X", "Z"), 'z': ("X", "Y")}
    legend_handles = []
    for group in frame.structural_groups:
        legend_handles.append(plt.Line2D([0], [0], color='black', lw=0, label=rf"$\bf{{{group.name}}}$"))
        for elem in group.structural_elements:
            legend_handles.append(plt.Line2D([0], [0], color=elem.color, lw=3, label=f"{elem.name}"))

    # add faults header + lines
    if frame.fault_frame is not None and frame.fault_frame.fault_elements:
        legend_handles.append(plt.Line2D([0], [0], color='black', lw=0, label=rf"$\bf{{Faults}}$"))
        for fault in frame.fault_frame.fault_elements:
            fcol = fault.color or "black"
            legend_handles.append(plt.Line2D([0], [0], color=fcol, lw=3, label=fault.name))

    by_label = {h.get_label(): h for h in legend_handles}
    ax.legend(by_label.values(), by_label.keys(), loc='center left', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.5), fontsize=8,
              frameon=True)

    ax.set_xlabel(axis_labels[axis][0])
    ax.set_ylabel(axis_labels[axis][1])
    base_title = f"{axis.upper()} Slice @ index {index}"
    ax.set_title(f"{base_title} — {title_suffix}" if title_suffix else base_title)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.set_xlim(extent[0], extent[1])
    ax.set_ylim(extent[2], extent[3])

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

def plot_structural_model_3D(
        frame: StructuralFrame,
        *,
        mesh_type: GeoMeshType = GeoMeshType.MASKED,
        fault_mesh_type: Optional[FaultMeshType] = None,
        show_surface_meshes: bool = True,
        show_points: bool = True,
        show_orientations: bool = True,
        fault_opacity: float = 0.35,
        show_lith_block: bool = False,
        notebook: bool = False,
        off_screen: bool = False,
        show: bool = True,
) -> pv.Plotter:
    """
    3D PyVista plot of a structural model with per-element meshes, input points, and faults.

    Parameters
    ----------
    frame : StructuralFrame
        Structural frame to visualize.
    mesh_type : GeoMeshType, default GeoMeshType.MASKED
        Mesh type for geological elements.
    fault_mesh_type : FaultMeshType, optional
        Mesh type for fault surfaces. Defaults to ``mesh_type`` if not set.
    show_surface_meshes : bool, default True
        Whether to render surface meshes for each element.
    show_points : bool, default True
        Whether to render input surface points.
    show_orientations : bool, default True
        Whether to render orientation arrows.
    fault_opacity : float, default 0.35
        Opacity of fault surface meshes.
    show_lith_block : bool, default False
        Show the lithology block as the outside of the model: the faces of the
        result cells on the six walls of the extent, colored by lithology, with
        their edges, so the grid's cells (uniform voxels, or octree cells of
        different sizes) are visible. The block hides what lies inside it.
    notebook : bool, default False
        Use off-screen/notebook mode for PyVista.
    off_screen : bool, default False
        Render off-screen (no window). Required for screenshot() without calling show() first.
    show : bool, default True
        Call plotter.show() at the end. Set False to add further actors before displaying.

    Returns
    -------
    pv.Plotter
        The PyVista plotter instance (useful when show=False).
    """
    fault_mesh_type_requested = fault_mesh_type is not None
    fault_mesh_type = fault_mesh_type if fault_mesh_type is not None else mesh_type

    pv.global_theme.allow_empty_mesh = True
    plotter = pv.Plotter(notebook=notebook, off_screen=off_screen)

    # ---------- plot structural meshes, points, orientations ----------
    legend_entries = []  # [(group_name, [(• elem, color), ...]), ...] in youngest->oldest order
    computed = frame.lith_block is not None and np.size(frame.lith_block) > 0
    drew_surface = False

    for group in frame.structural_groups:  # order preserved: youngest->oldest
        group_entries = []
        for elem in group.structural_elements:
            # legend entry
            group_entries.append((f"• {elem.name}", elem.color))

            # meshes (per domain)
            if show_surface_meshes:
                if mesh_type in elem.vertices and mesh_type in elem.edges:
                    drew_surface = True
                    plotter.add_mesh(
                        pv.PolyData(elem.vertices[mesh_type],
                                    np.insert(elem.edges[mesh_type], 0, 3, axis=1).ravel()),
                        color=elem.color, opacity=1.0, label=f"{group.name} | {elem.name}")

            # surface points
            if show_points and hasattr(frame, "get_surface_points_for_element"):
                df_points = frame.get_surface_points_for_element(elem.name)
                if df_points is not None and not df_points.empty:
                    cloud = pv.PolyData(df_points[["X", "Y", "Z"]].values.astype(np.float32))
                    plotter.add_points(cloud, color=elem.color, point_size=8, render_points_as_spheres=True)

            # orientations
            if show_orientations and frame.orientations is not None and hasattr(frame,
                                                                                                  "get_orientations_for_element"):
                df_ori = frame.get_orientations_for_element(elem.name)
                if df_ori is not None and not df_ori.empty:
                    start = df_ori[["X", "Y", "Z"]].values
                    direction = df_ori[["G_x", "G_y", "G_z"]].values
                    scale = _orientation_arrow_length(frame.grid, start)
                    for i in range(len(start)):
                        arrow = pv.Arrow(start=start[i], direction=direction[i], scale=scale)
                        plotter.add_mesh(arrow, color=elem.color)

        legend_entries.append((group.name, group_entries))

    if show_surface_meshes and computed and not drew_surface:
        available = sorted({str(t) for g in frame.structural_groups for e in g.structural_elements
                            for t in e.vertices})
        warnings.warn(
            f"mesh_type={mesh_type.value!r}: no element has this surface mesh"
            + (f"; available: {', '.join(available)}." if available
               else "; the model was computed without surface meshes (extract_meshes=False).")
            + " Plotting without surfaces.", stacklevel=2)

    # ---------- plot fault meshes ----------
    if frame.fault_frame is not None:
        # add a "Faults" header in legend (bold/black achievable only approximately in pyvista legend)
        faults_header = ("Faults", "black")
        # we'll append "Faults" header at the top with the flatten stage below
        fault_entries = []

        for fault in frame.fault_frame.fault_elements:
            if fault_mesh_type not in fault.vertices or fault_mesh_type not in fault.edges:
                if fault_mesh_type_requested:  # the default follows mesh_type and may have no fault equivalent
                    warnings.warn(
                        f"fault_mesh_type={fault_mesh_type.value!r}: fault '{fault.name}' has no such mesh "
                        f"(fault MASKED and EXTENDED_MASKED exist only after compute_structural_model); "
                        f"showing UNMASKED instead.", stacklevel=2)
                    fault_mesh_type_requested = False  # warn once
                fault_mesh_type = FaultMeshType.UNMASKED  # fallback if requested type not present
            fv = fault.vertices[fault_mesh_type]
            ff = fault.edges[fault_mesh_type]
            if fv is None or ff is None or len(fv) == 0 or len(ff) == 0:
                continue
            faces_flat = _faces_to_vtk(np.asarray(ff))
            try:
                fmesh = pv.PolyData(np.asarray(fv), faces_flat)
            except Exception:
                fmesh = pv.PolyData(np.asarray(fv), faces_flat.astype(np.int64, copy=False))
            fcolor = fault.color or "black"
            plotter.add_mesh(
                fmesh,
                color=fcolor,
                opacity=fault_opacity,
                label=f"Fault: {fault.name}"
            )
            fault_entries.append((f"• {fault.name}", fcolor))

        # prepend a header row
        legend_entries = [("Faults", fault_entries)] + legend_entries

    # ---------- lithology block: the cell faces on the outer walls ----------
    if show_lith_block and computed:
        plotter.add_mesh(_wall_faces(frame), scalars="rgb", rgb=True, show_edges=True,
                         edge_color="#333333", line_width=0.5)
    elif show_lith_block:
        warnings.warn("show_lith_block=True: there is no lithology block before the structural model has been "
                      "computed (compute_structural_model); plotting without it.", stacklevel=2)
        show_lith_block = False  # no basement legend entry either

    # ---------- legend like before (youngest at top; group bold-ish) ----------
    # flatten & reverse (PyVista renders top-down)
    flat_legend = []
    for group_name, entries in legend_entries:
        flat_legend.append((f"{group_name}", "black"))
        for label, col in entries:
            flat_legend.append((label, col))
    if show_lith_block:
        flat_legend.append(("• Basement", BASEMENT_COLOR))

    plotter.add_legend(labels=flat_legend, size=(0.22, 0.22), loc="lower right", face="rectangle")

    # bounds/grid + camera
    if frame.grid is not None:
        plotter.show_bounds(bounds=frame.grid.extent, location="furthest", grid=True)

    plotter.camera.view_angle = 30.0
    plotter.camera.azimuth = 25.0
    plotter.camera.elevation = -15.0

    if show:
        plotter.show()
    return plotter

class FaultElement(BaseModel):
    """
    Represents a geological fault surface to be interpolated.

    Notes:
        This model intentionally stores many fields in PrivateAttr (numpy arrays, sets)
        to avoid Pydantic overhead.

    Publicly exposed properties provide read-only access.
    """

    name: str = Field()
    scalar_value: Optional[float] = Field(default=None)
    scalar_field: Optional[NpNDArrayFp64] = Field(default=None)
    extended_scalar_field: Optional[NpNDArrayFp64] = Field(default=None)
    color: str = Field(default="#AAAAAA")  # Default color in hex format
    separated_domains: Optional[Tuple[FrozenSet[int], FrozenSet[int]]] = Field(
        default=None
    )
    domain_pairs: Optional[FrozenSet[Tuple[int, int]]] = Field(default=None)
    vertices: Dict[str, NpNDArrayFp64] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    edges: Dict[str, NpNDArrayInt32] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    mask: Optional[NpNDArrayBool] = Field(default=None)

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        # shortcut definition - not sure if I like this
        if args:
          if len(args) == 1 or len(args) == 2:
            kwargs["name"] = args[0]
          else:
            raise TypeError("Unsupported shortcut, name:str, scalar_value: Optional[float] = None ")
          if len(args) == 2:
            kwargs["scalar_value"] = args[1]
        super().__init__(**kwargs)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"FaultElement(name='{self.name}')"


    def set_scalar_field(self, scalar_field: NpNDArrayFp64) -> None:
        """Assign the interpolated scalar field values on the fault surface."""
        if not isinstance(scalar_field, np.ndarray):
            raise ValueError("Scalar field must be a numpy array.")
        self.scalar_field = scalar_field

    def set_scalar_value(self, value: float) -> None:
        """Assign scalar value used for interpolation."""
        self.scalar_value = value

    def set_color(self, color: str) -> None:
        """Set the display color for this fault in hex format."""
        if not isinstance(color, str) or not color.startswith("#") or len(color) != 7:
            raise ValueError("Color must be a valid hex string (e.g., '#RRGGBB').")
        self.color = color

    def set_mesh(
            self,
            mesh_type: FaultMeshType,
            vertices: npt.NDArray[np.generic],
            edges: npt.NDArray[np.generic],
    ) -> None:
        """
        Set the vertices and edges for a specific mesh type.

        Args:
            mesh_type: A ``FaultMeshType`` member.
            vertices: Vertex array.
            edges: Edge/connectivity array.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If mesh_type is not a valid ``FaultMeshType``.
        """
        try:
            mesh_type = FaultMeshType(mesh_type)
        except ValueError:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid mesh type '{mesh_type}'. Allowed types are: {', '.join(e.value for e in FaultMeshType)}."
            )
        self.vertices[mesh_type] = vertices
        self.edges[mesh_type] = edges

    def get_mesh(
            self, mesh_type: FaultMeshType
    ) -> tuple[npt.NDArray[np.generic], npt.NDArray[np.generic]]:
        """
        Retrieve the vertices and edges for the given mesh type.

        Raises:
            KeyError: If the mesh type does not exist.
        """
        try:
            return self.vertices[mesh_type], self.edges[mesh_type]
        except KeyError:
            raise KeyError(f"Mesh '{mesh_type}' not found in element '{self.name}'.")

    def set_domain_mask(self, mask: NpNDArrayBool) -> None:
        """
        Store the boolean mask (True/False) separating two fault blocks.
        """
        if not isinstance(mask, np.ndarray) or mask.dtype != bool:
            raise ValueError("Mask must be a boolean NumPy array.")
        self.mask = mask

    def get_domain_mask(self) -> NpNDArrayBool:
        """
        Retrieve the fault mask (True = one block, False = other).

        Raises:
            ValueError: If no mask has been set.
        """
        if self.mask is None:
            raise ValueError(f"No mask set for fault '{self.name}'.")
        return self.mask

    def get_inverse_domain_mask(self) -> NpNDArrayBool:
        """
        Get the inverse of the fault mask (opposite block).
        """
        return ~self.get_domain_mask()

    def get_separated_domains(self) -> Optional[Tuple[FrozenSet[int], FrozenSet[int]]]:
        """Get the tuple of separated domain IDs, if any."""
        return self.separated_domains

    def set_separated_domains(
            self, domain_ids: Tuple[FrozenSet[int], FrozenSet[int]]
    ) -> None:
        """Set the tuple of separated domain IDs."""
        self.separated_domains = domain_ids

    def get_domain_pairs(self) -> Optional[FrozenSet[Tuple[int, int]]]:
        """Return adjacent domain-id pairs across this fault surface."""
        return self.domain_pairs

    def set_domain_pairs(self, pairs: FrozenSet[Tuple[int, int]]) -> None:
        """
        Set adjacent domain-id pairs across this fault surface.

        Each pair must be (a, b) with a != b. Order will be normalized to (min, max).
        """
        if pairs is None:
            self.domain_pairs = None
            return

        if not isinstance(pairs, frozenset):
            pairs = frozenset(pairs)  # allow set/list input

        norm: set[Tuple[int, int]] = set()
        for p in pairs:
            if not (isinstance(p, tuple) and len(p) == 2):
                raise ValueError("Each domain pair must be a tuple (a, b).")
            a, b = int(p[0]), int(p[1])
            if a == b:
                continue
            norm.add((a, b) if a < b else (b, a))

        if not norm:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Fault '{self.name}' domain_pairs is empty after normalization."
            )

        self.domain_pairs = frozenset(norm)

    def domain_pairs_flat(self) -> set[int]:
        """Return all domain IDs touched by this fault's adjacency pairs."""
        if self.domain_pairs is None:
            return set()
        out: set[int] = set()
        for a, b in self.domain_pairs:
            out.add(a)
            out.add(b)
        return out

    def separated_domains_flat(self) -> set[int]:
        """Return all domain IDs this fault splits (from separated_domains)."""
        if self.separated_domains is None:
            return set()
        return set().union(*self.separated_domains)
